name: JLFloat32Vector
doc: This domain provides a fast JLFloat32 vector type with no bound checking on elt's. Minimum index is 1.
#(u) returns the number of elements in u.

name: any?
doc: any?(p, u) tests if p(x) is true for any element x of u. Note: for collections, any?(p, u) = reduce(or, map(p, u), false , true). However, any?(p, u) returns as soon as it finds an element for which p gives true.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(x) allows Segment values to be used as %.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(a) transforms a into an element of S.

name: concat
doc: concat(u, v) returns an aggregate consisting of the elements of u followed by the elements of v. Note: if w = concat(u, v) then w.i = u.i for i in indices u and w.(j + maxIndex u) = v.j for j in indices v.

name: concat
doc: concat(u, x) returns aggregate u with additional element x at the end. Note: for lists, concat(u, x) = concat(u, [x]).

name: concat
doc: concat(x, u) returns aggregate u with additional element x at the front. Note: for lists: concat(x, u) = concat([x], u).

name: concat
doc: concat(u), where u is a list of aggregates [a, b, ..., c], returns a single aggregate consisting of the elements of a fo llowed by those of b followed ... by the elements of c. Note: concat([a, b, ..., c]) = concat(a, concat([b, ..., c])).

name: construct
doc: construct([x, y, ..., z]) returns the collection of elements x, y, ..., z ordered as given. Equivalently written as [x, y, ..., z]$D, where D is the domain. D may be omitted for those of type List.

name: copy
doc: copy(u) returns a top-level (non-recursive) copy of u. Note: for collections, copy(u) = [x for x in u].

name: copy!
doc: copy!(b,a) efficiently copies a to b. No checks are performed on array dimensions.

name: copyInto!
doc: copyInto!(u, v, i) returns aggregate u containing a copy of v inserted at element i.

name: count
doc: count(x, u) returns the number of occurrences of x in u. For collections, count(x, u) = reduce(+, [1 for y in u | x = y] , 0).

name: count
doc: count(p, u) returns the number of elements x in u such that p(x) is true. For collections, count(p, u) = reduce(+, [1 fo r x in u | p(x)], 0).

name: cross
doc: cross(u, v) constructs the cross product of u and v. Error: if u and v are not of length 3.

name: delete
doc: delete(u, i) returns a copy of u with the ith element deleted. Note: delete(u, i) = concat(u(minIndex(u)..i - 1), u(i + 1..)).

name: delete
doc: delete(u, i..j) returns a copy of u with the ith through jth element deleted. Note: delete(u, i..j) = concat(u(minIndex( u)..i-1), u(j+1..)).

name: dot
doc: dot(f) creates the form with one dot overhead.

name: dot
doc: dot(f, n) creates the form f with n dots overhead.

name: dot
doc: dot(x, y) computes the inner product of the two vectors x and y. Error: if x and y are not of the same length.

name: elt
doc: elt(op, l) creates a form for application of op to list of arguments l.

name: elt
doc: elt(u, i) (also written: u.i) returns the element of u indexed by i. Error: if i is not an index of u.

name: elt
doc: elt(u, x, y) applies u to x if x is in the domain of u, and returns y otherwise.

name: empty
doc: empty()$D creates an aggregate of type D with 0 elements. Note: The  $D can be dropped if understood by context, e.g. u: D := empty().

name: empty?
doc: empty?(u) tests if u has 0 elements.

name: entries
doc: entries(u) returns a list of all the entries of aggregate u in no assumed order.

name: entry?
doc: entry?(x, u) tests if x equals u . i for some index i.

name: eq?
doc: eq?(u, v) tests if u and v are same objects.

name: every?
doc: every?(p, u) tests if p(x) is true for all elements x of u. Note: for collections, every?(p, u) = reduce(and, map(p, u), true, false). However, every?(p, u) returns as soon as it finds an element for which p gives false.

name: exprand
doc: exprand(n) returns a vector of size n with random elements from the exponential distribution with scale 1.

name: fill!
doc: fill!(u, x) replaces each entry in aggregate u by x. The modified u is returned as value.

name: find
doc: find(p, u) returns the first x in u such that p(x) is true, and "failed" otherwise.

name: first
doc: first(u, n) returns a copy of the first n elements of u. Error: if u has less than n elements.

name: first
doc: first(u) returns the first element x of u. Note: for collections, first([x, y, ..., z]) = x. Error: if u is empty.

name: index?
doc: index?(i, u) tests if i is an index of aggregate u.

name: indices
doc: indices(u) returns a list of indices of aggregate u in no particular order.

name: insert
doc: insert(v, u, i) returns a copy of u having v inserted beginning at the ith element. Note: insert(v, u, i) = concat(u(min Index(u)..i-1), concat(v, u(i..))).

name: insert
doc: insert(x, u, i) returns a copy of u having x as its ith element. Note: insert(x, u, i) = concat(u(minIndex(u)..i-1), con cat(x, u(i..))).

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, v) applies func to argument v.

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, v) applies func to argument v. and returns a Julia Float32.

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, v) applies func to argument v. and returns a JLFloat32Vector.

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, v, val) applies func to arguments v and val and returns a Julia Float32.

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, v1, v2) applies func to arguments v1 and v2.

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, v1, v2, v3) applies func to arguments v1, v2 and v3.

name: jlApprox?
doc: jlApprox?(x,y) computes inexact equality comparison with default parameters. Two numbers compare equal if their relative distance or their absolute distance is within tolerance bounds. Applied component-wise.

name: jlDisplay
doc: jlDisplay(v) pretty prints v (à la Julia).

name: juliaVPrint
doc: juliaVPrint(b) defines whether or not FriCAS uses the printing version of Julia for vectors instead of its OutputForm version. Returns previous value. By default it is the Julia version.

name: latex
doc: latex(s) returns a LaTeX-printable output representation of s.

name: leftTrim
doc: leftTrim(u, x) returns a copy of u with all leading x deleted. For example, leftTrim(" abc ", char " ") returns "abc ".

name: length
doc: length(v) computes the sqrt(dot(v, v)), i.e. the euclidean length

name: less?
doc: less?(u, n) tests if u has less than n elements.

name: map
doc: map(f, u) returns a copy of u with each element x replaced by f(x). For collections, map(f, u) = [f(x) for x in u].

name: map
doc: map(f, u, v) returns a new aggregate w with elements z = f(x, y) for corresponding elements x and y from u and v. Note: w.i = f(u.i, v.i).

name: map!
doc: map!(f, u) destructively replaces each element x of u by f(x).

name: max
doc: max(x,y) returns the maximum of x and y relative to "<".

name: max
doc: max(u) returns maximal element of u. Error if u is empty.

name: max
doc: max(p, u) returns maximal element of u with respect to total ordering predicate p. Error if u is empty.

name: maxIndex
doc: maxIndex(u) returns the maximum index i of aggregate u. Note: in general, maxIndex(u) = reduce(max, indices u); for List , maxIndex(u) = #u.

name: member?
doc: member?(x, u) tests if x is a member of u. For collections, member?(x, u) = reduce(or, [x=y for y in u], false). However , member?(x, u) returns as soon as it finds a member.

name: members
doc: members(u) returns a list of the consecutive elements of u. For multisets members gives result with no repetition. See a lso parts.

name: merge
doc: merge(u, v) merges u and v in ascending order. Note: merge(u, v) = merge(<=, u, v).

name: merge
doc: merge(p, a, b) returns an aggregate c which merges a and b. The result is produced by examining each element x of a and y of b successively. If p(x, y) is true, then x is inserted into the result; otherwise y is inserted. If x is chosen, th e next element of a is examined, and so on. When all the elements of one aggregate are examined, the remaining elements of the other are appended. For example, merge(<, [1, 3], [2, 7, 5]) returns [1, 2, 3, 7, 5].

name: merge_unique
doc: merge_unique(p, a, b) returns an aggregate c which merges a and b uniquely. p is a binary predicate and aggregates a and b are assumed to be ordered under p and without duplicates. The result aggregate c is also ordered under p, and contain s all elements from a and b, also without duplicates. For example, merge_unique(<, [1, 3, 5], [3, 5, 6]) returns [1, 3, 5, 6].

name: min
doc: min(x,y) returns the minimum of x and y relative to "<".

name: min
doc: min(u) returns minimal element of u. Error if u is empty.

name: minIndex
doc: minIndex(u) returns the minimum index i of aggregate u. Note: in general, minIndex(a) = reduce(min, indices a); for List , minIndex(a) = 1.

name: more?
doc: more?(u, n) tests if u has more than n elements.

name: new
doc: new(n, x) returns a new aggregate of size n all of whose entries are x.

name: nrand
doc: nrand(n) returns a normally distributed Julia vector of size n with mean=0 and standard deviation=1.

name: outerProduct
doc: outerProduct(u, v) constructs the matrix whose (i, j)'th element is u(i)*v(j).

name: parts
doc: parts(u) returns a list of the consecutive elements of u. For finite collections, construct(parts(u)) = u.

name: position
doc: position(x, a) returns the index i of the first occurrence of x in a, and minIndex(a) - 1 if there is no such x.

name: position
doc: position(x, a, n) returns the index i of the first occurrence of x in a where i >= n, and minIndex(a) - 1 if no such x i s found.

name: position
doc: position(p, a) returns the index i of the first x in a such that p(x) is true, and minIndex(a) - 1 if there is no such x .

name: qelt
doc: qelt(u, x) applies u to x without checking whether x is in the domain of u. If x is not in the domain of u a memory-acce ss violation may occur. If a check on whether x is in the domain of u is required, use the function elt.

name: qnew
doc: qnew(n) returns an uninitialized vector of dimension n.

name: qsetelt!
doc: qsetelt!(u, x, y) sets the image of x to be y under u, without checking that x is in the domain of u. If such a check is required use the function setelt!.

name: reduce
doc: reduce(f, u) reduces the binary operation f across u. For example, if u is [x, y, ..., z] then reduce(f, u) returns f(.. f(f(x, y), ...), z). Note: if u has one element x, reduce(f, u) returns x. Error: if u is empty.

name: reduce
doc: reduce(f, u, x) reduces the binary operation f across u, where x is the identity operation of f. Same as reduce(f, u) if u has 2 or more elements. Returns f(y, x) if u has one element y. Returns x if u is empty. For example, reduce(+, u, 0) returns the sum of the elements of u.

name: reduce
doc: reduce(f, u, x, z) reduces the binary operation f across u, stopping when an "absorbing element" z is encountered. As fo r reduce(f, u, x), x is the identity element of f. Same as reduce(f, u, x) when u contains no element z. Thus the third argument x is returned when u is empty.

name: remove
doc: remove(x, u) returns a copy of u with all elements equal to x removed. Note: remove(x, u) = [y for y in u | y ~= x].

name: remove
doc: remove(p, u) returns a copy of u removing all elements x such that p(x) is true. Note: remove(p, u) = [x for x in u | no t p(x)].

name: removeDuplicates
doc: removeDuplicates(u) returns a copy of u with all duplicates removed.

name: reverse
doc: reverse(a) returns a copy of a with elements in reverse order.

name: reverse!
doc: reverse!(u) returns u with its elements in reverse order.

name: rightTrim
doc: rightTrim(u, x) returns a copy of u with all trailing occurrences of x deleted. For example, rightTrim(" abc ", char " " ) returns " abc".

name: sample
doc: sample yields a value of type %

name: select
doc: select(p, u) returns a copy of u containing only those elements such p(x) is true. Note: select(p, u) = [x for x in u | p(x)].

name: setelt!
doc: setelt!(u, x, y) sets the image of x to be y under u, if x is in the domain of u. Error: if x is not in the domain of u.

name: setelt!
doc: setelt!(u, i..j, x) (also written: u(i..j) := x) destructively replaces each element in the segment u(i..j) by x. The va lue x is returned. Note: u is destructively changed so that u.k := x for k in i..j; its length remains unchanged.

name: size?
doc: size?(u, n) tests if u has exactly n elements.

name: smaller?
doc: smaller?(x, y) is a strict ordering on depending on representatives of elements of the set. If % has Comparable then sma ller? gives mathematical linear order.

name: sort
doc: sort(u) returns a copy of u with elements in ascending order. Note: sort(u) = sort(<, u).

name: sort
doc: sort(p, a) returns a copy of a sorted using total ordering predicate p.

name: sort!
doc: sort!(u) returns u with its elements in ascending order.

name: sort!
doc: sort!(p, u) returns u with its elements ordered by p.

name: sorted?
doc: sorted?(u) tests if the elements of u are in ascending order.

name: sorted?
doc: sorted?(p, a) tests if a is sorted according to predicate p.

name: swap!
doc: swap!(u, i, j) interchanges elements i and j of aggregate u. No meaningful value is returned.

name: trim
doc: trim(u, x) returns a copy of u with all occurrences of x deleted from right and left ends. For example, trim(" abc ", ch ar " ") returns "abc".

name: urand
doc: urand(n, x) returns a uniformly (0..x) distributed Julia vector of size n. Use the underlying Common Lisp random number generator so jlSeed! will not affect it.

name: urand01
doc: urand01(n) returns a uniformly (0..1) distributed Julia vector of size n.

name: vector
doc: vector(l) converts the list l to a vector.

name: zero
doc: zero(n) creates a zero vector of length n.

name: zero?
doc: zero?(x) returns true if x is a zero vector, false otherwise.

name: JLFloat32VectorFunctions2
doc: This package provides operations which all take as arguments JLFloat32Vector and functions from JLFloat32 to JLFloat32. The operations all iterate over their vector argument and either return a value of type JLFloat32Vector or a JLFloat32.

name: map
doc: map(f, v) applies the function f to every element of the vector v producing a new vector containing the values.

name: map
doc: map(f, v) applies the function f to every element of the vector v producing a new vector containing the values or \spad{"failed"}.

name: map
doc: map(f, v) applies the function f to every element of the vector v producing a new vector containing the values or "faile d".

name: reduce
doc: reduce(func, vec, ident) combines the elements in vec using the binary function func. Argument ident is returned if vec is empty.

name: scan
doc: scan(func, vec, ident) creates a new vector whose elements are the result of applying reduce to the binary function func, increasing initial subsequences of the vector vec, and the element ident.

name: scan
doc: scan(func, vec, ident) creates a new vector whose elements are the result of applying reduce to the binary function func , increasing initial subsequences of the vector vec, and the element ident.

name: JLFloat32Matrix
doc: This domain provides a fast JLFloat32 matrix type with no bound checking on elt's. Minimum index is 1.
#(u) returns the number of elements in u.

name: Pfaffian
doc: Pfaffian(m) returns the Pfaffian of the matrix m. Error: if the matrix is not antisymmetric.

name: antisymmetric?
doc: antisymmetric?(m) returns true if the matrix m is square and antisymmetric (i.e. m[i, j] = -m[j, i] for all i and j) and false otherwise.

name: any?
doc: any?(p, u) tests if p(x) is true for any element x of u. Note: for collections, any?(p, u) = reduce(or, map(p, u), false , true). However, any?(p, u) returns as soon as it finds an element for which p gives true.

name: array2
doc: array2(ll) constructs a 2-dimensional array, the inner list being the rows.

name: blockConcat
doc: blockConcat(ll) concatenates arrays row and column wise, building an array from blocks. The order is row major as in mat rix.

name: blockSplit
doc: blockSplit(a, [n1,...,ni], [m1,...,mi]) splits a into multiple subarrays row and column wise, such that element at posit ion k, l has nk rows and ml columns. Error: if number of rows of a is different than n1 + ... + ni or number of columns of a is different than m1 + ... + mj

name: blockSplit
doc: blockSplit(a, n, m) splits a into n*m subarrays of equal size row and column wise, dividing a into blocks. Error: if num ber of rows of a is not divisible by n or number of columns of a is not divisible by m.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(col) converts the column col to a column matrix.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(a) transforms a into an element of S.

name: colSlice
doc: colSlice(m) returns a segment s such that for m the access m(i, s) gives the i-th row.

name: column
doc: column(m, j) returns the jth column of m error check to determine if index is in proper ranges

name: columnSpace
doc: columnSpace(m) returns a sublist of columns of the matrix m forming a basis of its column space.

name: convert
doc: convert(a) transforms a into an element of S.

name: copy
doc: copy(u) returns a top-level (non-recursive) copy of u. Note: for collections, copy(u) = [x for x in u].

name: copy!
doc: copy!(b,a) efficiently copies a to b. No checks are performed on array dimensions.

name: count
doc: count(x, u) returns the number of occurrences of x in u. For collections, count(x, u) = reduce(+, [1 for y in u | x = y] , 0).

name: count
doc: count(p, u) returns the number of elements x in u such that p(x) is true. For collections, count(p, u) = reduce(+, [1 fo r x in u | p(x)], 0).

name: determinant
doc: determinant(m) returns the determinant of the matrix m. Error: if the matrix is not square.

name: diagonal?
doc: diagonal?(m) returns true if the matrix m is square and diagonal (i.e. all entries of m not on the diagonal are zero) an d false otherwise.

name: diagonalMatrix
doc: diagonalMatrix(v) returns a diagonal matrix with elements of v.

name: diagonalMatrix
doc: diagonalMatrix([m1, ..., mk]) creates a block diagonal matrix M with block matrices  m1, ...,  mk down the diagonal, wit h 0 block matrices elsewhere. More precisely: if ri := nrows mi, ci := ncols mi, then m is an (r1+..+rk) by (c1+..+ck) m atrix with entries m.i.j = ml.(i-r1-..-r(l-1)).(j-c1-..-c(l-1)), if (r1+..+r(l-1)) < i <= r1+..+rl and (c1+..+c(l-1)) < i <= c1+..+cl, m.i.j = 0 otherwise.

name: max

name: max

signature: (JLFloat32, %) -> Boolean if % has ATFINAG and JLFloat32 has BASTYPE
doc: member?(x, u) tests if x is a member of u. For collections, member?(x, u) = reduce(or, [x=y for y in u], false). However , member?(x, u) returns as soon as it finds a member.

name: members

name: min
signature: % -> JLFloat32 if % has ATFINAG and JLFloat32 has ORDSET
doc: min(u) returns minimal element of u. Error if u is empty.

name: minRowIndex

name: ncols

name: nrows

name: nullSpace
doc: nullSpace(m) returns a basis for the null space of the matrix m. Note: null space is considered as vector space over quo tient field of the ring.

name: nullity
doc: nullity(m) returns the nullity of the matrix m. This is the dimension of the null space of the matrix m.

name: one?

name: opposite?
doc: opposite?(x,y) holds if the sum of x and y is 0.

name: parts
doc: parts(u) returns a list of the consecutive elements of u. For finite collections, construct(parts(u)) = u.

name: plenaryPower

name: qcoerce

name: qelt
doc: qelt(m, i, j) returns the element in the ith row and jth column of the matrix m. Note: there is NO error check to determ ine if indices are in the proper ranges.

name: qelt
doc: qelt(m, i) returns the i-th element of m. Column major order.

name: random
doc: random(n) returns a random integer from 0 to n-1.

name: rank
doc: rank(m) returns the rank of the matrix m.

name: recip
doc: recip(a) returns an element, which is both a left and a right inverse of a, or "failed" if such an element doesn't exist or cannot be determined (see unitsKnown).

name: reducedSystem
doc: reducedSystem(A) returns a matrix B such that A x = 0 and B x = 0 have the same solutions in R.

name: reducedSystem
doc: reducedSystem(A, v) returns a matrix B and a vector w such that A x = v and B x = w have the same solutions in R.

name: retract
doc: retract(a) transforms a into an element of S if possible. Error: if a cannot be made into an element of S.

name: retractIfCan
doc: retractIfCan(a) transforms a into an element of S if possible. Returns "failed" if a cannot be made into an element of S .

name: rightPower
doc: rightPower(a, n) returns the n-th right power of a, i.e. rightPower(a, n) := rightPower(a, n-1) * a and rightPower(a, 0) := 1.

name: rightPower
doc: rightPower(a, n) returns the n-th right power of a, i.e. rightPower(a, n) := rightPower(a, n-1) * a and rightPower(a, 1) := a.

name: rightRecip
doc: rightRecip(a) returns an element, which is a right inverse of a, or "failed" if such an element doesn't exist or cannot be determined (see unitsKnown).

name: row
doc: row(m, i) returns the ith row of the matrix m. Error: if the index is outside the proper range.

name: rowEchelon
doc: rowEchelon(m) returns the row echelon form of the matrix m.

name: sample
doc: sample yields a value of type %

name: scalarMatrix
doc: scalarMatrix(r) returns an n-by-n matrix with r's on the diagonal and zeroes elsewhere.

name: size?
doc: size?(u, n) tests if u has exactly n elements.

name: square?
doc: square?(m) returns true if m is a square matrix (i.e. if m has the same number of rows as columns) and false otherwise.

name: squareMatrix
doc: squareMatrix(m) returns a copy of m as a JLF32SquareMatrix.

name: string
doc: string(jt) returns the string representation of jt.

name: subtractIfCan
signature: (%, %) -> Union(%,"failed") if % has ABELGRP or Integer has ABELGRP and JLFloat32 has LINEXP(INT) and JLFloat32 has RING or JLFloat32 has ABELGRP
doc: subtractIfCan(x, y) returns an element z such that z+y=x or "failed" if no such element exists.

name: symmetric?
doc: symmetric?(m) returns true if the matrix m is square and symmetric (i.e. m[i, j] = m[j, i] for all i and j) and false ot herwise.

name: trace
doc: trace(m) returns the trace of the matrix m. This is the sum of the elements on the diagonal of the matrix m.

name: zero?
doc: zero?(m) returns true if m is a zero matrix and false otherwise

name: coerce
doc: coerce(x) allows Segment values to be used as %.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(a) transforms a into an element of S.

name: concat
doc: concat(u, v) returns an aggregate consisting of the elements of u followed by the elements of v. Note: if w = concat(u, v) then w.i = u.i for i in indices u and w.(j + maxIndex u) = v.j for j in indices v.

name: concat
doc: concat(u, x) returns aggregate u with additional element x at the end. Note: for lists, concat(u, x) = concat(u, [x]).

name: concat
doc: concat(x, u) returns aggregate u with additional element x at the front. Note: for lists: concat(x, u) = concat([x], u).

name: concat
doc: concat(u), where u is a list of aggregates [a, b, ..., c], returns a single aggregate consisting of the elements of a fo llowed by those of b followed ... by the elements of c. Note: concat([a, b, ..., c]) = concat(a, concat([b, ..., c])).

name: construct
doc: construct([x, y, ..., z]) returns the collection of elements x, y, ..., z ordered as given. Equivalently written as [x, y, ..., z]$D, where D is the domain. D may be omitted for those of type List.

name: copy
doc: copy(u) returns a top-level (non-recursive) copy of u. Note: for collections, copy(u) = [x for x in u].

name: copy!
doc: copy!(b,a) efficiently copies a to b. No checks are performed on array dimensions.

name: copyInto!
doc: copyInto!(u, v, i) returns aggregate u containing a copy of v inserted at element i.

name: count
doc: count(x, u) returns the number of occurrences of x in u. For collections, count(x, u) = reduce(+, [1 for y in u | x = y] , 0).

name: count
doc: count(p, u) returns the number of elements x in u such that p(x) is true. For collections, count(p, u) = reduce(+, [1 fo r x in u | p(x)], 0).

name: cross
doc: cross(u, v) constructs the cross product of u and v. Error: if u and v are not of length 3.

name: delete
doc: delete(u, i) returns a copy of u with the ith element deleted. Note: delete(u, i) = concat(u(minIndex(u)..i - 1), u(i + 1..)).

name: delete
doc: delete(u, i..j) returns a copy of u with the ith through jth element deleted. Note: delete(u, i..j) = concat(u(minIndex( u)..i-1), u(j+1..)).

name: dot
doc: dot(f) creates the form with one dot overhead.

name: dot
doc: dot(f, n) creates the form f with n dots overhead.

name: dot
doc: dot(x, y) computes the inner product of the two vectors x and y. Error: if x and y are not of the same length.

name: elt
doc: elt(op, l) creates a form for application of op to list of arguments l.

name: elt
doc: elt(u, i) (also written: u.i) returns the element of u indexed by i. Error: if i is not an index of u.

name: elt
doc: elt(u, x, y) applies u to x if x is in the domain of u, and returns y otherwise.

name: empty
doc: empty()$D creates an aggregate of type D with 0 elements. Note: The  $D can be dropped if understood by context, e.g. u: D := empty().

name: empty?
doc: empty?(u) tests if u has 0 elements.

name: entries
doc: entries(u) returns a list of all the entries of aggregate u in no assumed order.

name: entry?
doc: entry?(x, u) tests if x equals u . i for some index i.

name: eq?
doc: eq?(u, v) tests if u and v are same objects.

name: every?
doc: every?(p, u) tests if p(x) is true for all elements x of u. Note: for collections, every?(p, u) = reduce(and, map(p, u), true, false). However, every?(p, u) returns as soon as it finds an element for which p gives false.

name: fill!
doc: fill!(u, x) replaces each entry in aggregate u by x. The modified u is returned as value.

name: find
doc: find(p, u) returns the first x in u such that p(x) is true, and "failed" otherwise.

name: first
doc: first(u, n) returns a copy of the first n elements of u. Error: if u has less than n elements.

name: first
doc: first(u) returns the first element x of u. Note: for collections, first([x, y, ..., z]) = x. Error: if u is empty.

name: imag
doc: imag(v) returns a JLFloat32 vector with the imaginary part of the v elements.

name: index?
doc: index?(i, u) tests if i is an index of aggregate u.

name: indices
doc: indices(u) returns a list of indices of aggregate u in no particular order.

name: insert
doc: insert(v, u, i) returns a copy of u having v inserted beginning at the ith element. Note: insert(v, u, i) = concat(u(min Index(u)..i-1), concat(v, u(i..))).

name: insert
doc: insert(x, u, i) returns a copy of u having x as its ith element. Note: insert(x, u, i) = concat(u(minIndex(u)..i-1), con cat(x, u(i..))).

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, x) applies func to argument x.

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, x) applies func to argument x.

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, x, val) applies func to arguments x and val.

name: jlApprox?
doc: jlApprox?(x,y) computes inexact equality comparison with default parameters. Two numbers compare equal if their relative distance or their absolute distance is within tolerance bounds. Applied component-wise.

name: jlDisplay
doc: jlDisplay(v) pretty prints v (à la Julia).

name: juliaCVPrint
doc: juliaCVPrint(b) defines whether or not FriCAS uses the printing version of Julia for matrices instead of its OutputForm version. Returns previous value. By default it is the Julia version.

name: latex
doc: latex(s) returns a LaTeX-printable output representation of s.

name: leftTrim
doc: leftTrim(u, x) returns a copy of u with all leading x deleted. For example, leftTrim(" abc ", char " ") returns "abc ".

name: length
doc: length(v) computes the sqrt(dot(v, v)), i.e. the euclidean length

name: less?
doc: less?(u, n) tests if u has less than n elements.

name: map
doc: map(f, u) returns a copy of u with each element x replaced by f(x). For collections, map(f, u) = [f(x) for x in u].

name: map
doc: map(f, u, v) returns a new aggregate w with elements z = f(x, y) for corresponding elements x and y from u and v. Note: w.i = f(u.i, v.i).

name: map!
doc: map!(f, u) destructively replaces each element x of u by f(x).

name: max
doc: max(u) returns maximal element of u. Error if u is empty.

name: max
doc: max(p, u) returns maximal element of u with respect to total ordering predicate p. Error if u is empty.

name: maxIndex
doc: maxIndex(u) returns the maximum index i of aggregate u. Note: in general, maxIndex(u) = reduce(max, indices u); for List , maxIndex(u) = #u.

name: member?
doc: member?(x, u) tests if x is a member of u. For collections, member?(x, u) = reduce(or, [x=y for y in u], false). However , member?(x, u) returns as soon as it finds a member.

name: members
doc: members(u) returns a list of the consecutive elements of u. For multisets members gives result with no repetition. See a lso parts.

name: merge
doc: merge(u, v) merges u and v in ascending order. Note: merge(u, v) = merge(<=, u, v).

name: merge
doc: merge(p, a, b) returns an aggregate c which merges a and b. The result is produced by examining each element x of a and y of b successively. If p(x, y) is true, then x is inserted into the result; otherwise y is inserted. If x is chosen, th e next element of a is examined, and so on. When all the elements of one aggregate are examined, the remaining elements of the other are appended. For example, merge(<, [1, 3], [2, 7, 5]) returns [1, 2, 3, 7, 5].

name: merge_unique
doc: merge_unique(p, a, b) returns an aggregate c which merges a and b uniquely. p is a binary predicate and aggregates a and b are assumed to be ordered under p and without duplicates. The result aggregate c is also ordered under p, and contain s all elements from a and b, also without duplicates. For example, merge_unique(<, [1, 3, 5], [3, 5, 6]) returns [1, 3, 5, 6].

name: minIndex
doc: minIndex(u) returns the minimum index i of aggregate u. Note: in general, minIndex(a) = reduce(min, indices a); for List , minIndex(a) = 1.

name: more?
doc: more?(u, n) tests if u has more than n elements.

name: new

name: nrand
doc: nrand(n) returns a normally distributed Julia vector of size n with mean=0 and standard deviation=1. See Julia documentation (randn) for this complex version used here.

name: outerProduct
doc: outerProduct(u, v) constructs the matrix whose (i, j)'th element is u(i)*v(j).

name: parts
doc: parts(u) returns a list of the consecutive elements of u. For finite collections, construct(parts(u)) = u.

name: position

name: position
doc: position(x, a, n) returns the index i of the first occurrence of x in a where i >= n, and minIndex(a) - 1 if no such x i s found.

name: position
doc: position(p, a) returns the index i of the first x in a such that p(x) is true, and minIndex(a) - 1 if there is no such x .

name: qelt

name: qnew

name: qsetelt!

name: real

name: reduce
doc: reduce(f, u) reduces the binary operation f across u. For example, if u is [x, y, ..., z] then reduce(f, u) returns f(.. f(f(x, y), ...), z). Note: if u has one element x, reduce(f, u) returns x. Error: if u is empty.

name: reduce
doc: reduce(f, u, x) reduces the binary operation f across u, where x is the identity operation of f. Same as reduce(f, u) if u has 2 or more elements. Returns f(y, x) if u has one element y. Returns x if u is empty. For example, reduce(+, u, 0) returns the sum of the elements of u.

name: reduce
doc: reduce(f, u, x, z) reduces the binary operation f across u, stopping when an "absorbing element" z is encountered. As fo r reduce(f, u, x), x is the identity element of f. Same as reduce(f, u, x) when u contains no element z. Thus the third argument x is returned when u is empty.

name: remove
doc: remove(x, u) returns a copy of u with all elements equal to x removed. Note: remove(x, u) = [y for y in u | y ~= x].

name: remove
doc: remove(p, u) returns a copy of u removing all elements x such that p(x) is true. Note: remove(p, u) = [x for x in u | no t p(x)].

name: removeDuplicates
doc: removeDuplicates(u) returns a copy of u with all duplicates removed.

name: reverse

name: reverse!

doc: sample yields a value of type %

name: setelt!

name: setelt!

name: size?

name: smaller?

name: sort
doc: sort(u) returns a copy of u with elements in ascending order. Note: sort(u) = sort(<, u).

name: sort

name: sort!
doc: sort!(u) returns u with its elements in ascending order.

name: sort!
doc: sort!(p, u) returns u with its elements ordered by p.

name: sorted?
doc: sorted?(u) tests if the elements of u are in ascending order.

name: sorted?
doc: sorted?(p, a) tests if a is sorted according to predicate p.

name: swap!
doc: swap!(u, i, j) interchanges elements i and j of aggregate u. No meaningful value is returned.

name: trim

doc: zero?(x) returns true if x is a zero vector, false otherwise.

name: adjoint
doc: adjoint(m) returns the adjoint of m i.e. the conjugate transposition of m.

name: adjoint!
doc: adjoint!(a, m) stores in a the adjoint of m i.e. the conjugate transposition of m.

name: antisymmetric?
doc: antisymmetric?(m) returns true if the matrix m is square and antisymmetric (i.e. m[i, j] = -m[j, i] for all i and j) and false otherwise.

name: any?
doc: any?(p, u) tests if p(x) is true for any element x of u. Note: for collections, any?(p, u) = reduce(or, map(p, u), false , true). However, any?(p, u) returns as soon as it finds an element for which p gives true.

name: array2

name: blockConcat

name: blockSplit
doc: blockSplit(a, [n1,...,ni], [m1,...,mi]) splits a into multiple subarrays row and column wise, such that element at posit ion k, l has nk rows and ml columns. Error: if number of rows of a is different than n1 + ... + ni or number of columns of a is different than m1 + ... + mj

name: blockSplit
doc: blockSplit(a, n, m) splits a into n*m subarrays of equal size row and column wise, dividing a into blocks. Error: if num ber of rows of a is not divisible by n or number of columns of a is not divisible by m.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(m) coerces m to a Julia Complex Float 32 matrix.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(col) converts the column col to a column matrix.

name: coerce

name: colSlice
doc: colSlice(m) returns a segment s such that for m the access m(i, s) gives the i-th row.

name: column

name: count
doc: count(x, u) returns the number of occurrences of x in u. For collections, count(x, u) = reduce(+, [1 for y in u | x = y] , 0).

name: count
doc: count(p, u) returns the number of elements x in u such that p(x) is true. For collections, count(p, u) = reduce(+, [1 fo r x in u | p(x)], 0).

name: determinant
doc: determinant(m) returns the determinant of the matrix m. Error: if the matrix is not square.

name: diagonal?
doc: diagonal?(m) returns true if the matrix m is square and diagonal (i.e. all entries of m not on the diagonal are zero) an d false otherwise.

name: diagonalMatrix
doc: diagonalMatrix(v) returns a diagonal matrix with elements of v.

name: diagonalMatrix
doc: diagonalMatrix([m1, ..., mk]) creates a block diagonal matrix M with block matrices  m1, ...,  mk down the diagonal, wit h 0 block matrices elsewhere. More precisely: if ri := nrows mi, ci := ncols mi, then m is an (r1+..+rk) by (c1+..+ck) m atrix with entries m.i.j = ml.(i-r1-..-r(l-1)).(j-c1-..-c(l-1)), if (r1+..+r(l-1)) < i <= r1+..+rl and (c1+..+c(l-1)) < i <= c1+..+cl, m.i.j = 0 otherwise.

name: diagonalMatrix
doc: diagonalMatrix(l) returns a diagonal matrix with the elements of l on the diagonal.

name: elt
doc: elt(m, i) returns the i-th element of m. Column major order.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, row, colList) returns an 1-by-n array consisting of elements of x, where n = # colList. If colList = [j<1>, j<2>, ..., j<n>], then the (k, l)th entry of elt(x, row, colList) is x(row, j<l>).

name: elt
doc: elt(x, row, ls2) is equivalent to elt(x, row, l2) where l2 is obtained by appending expansions of elements of ls2, but s hould be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt

name: elt
doc: elt(x, rowList, s) is equivalent to elt(x, rowList, expand(s)) but should be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, ls1, col) is equivalent to elt(x, l1, col) where l1 is obtained by appending expansions of elements of ls1, but s hould be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, ls1, ls2) is equivalent to elt(x, l1, l2) where li is obtained by appending expansions of elements of lsi, but sh ould be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, ls1, s2) is equivalent to elt(x, l1, l2) where li is obtained by appending expansions of elements of lsi, but sho uld be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, s, colList) is equivalent to elt(x, expand(s), colList) but should be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, s1, ls2) is equivalent to elt(x, l1, l2) where li is obtained by appending expansions of elements of lsi, but sho uld be more convenient and more efficient.

doc: elt(x, s1, s2) is equivalent to elt(x, expand(s1), expand(s2)) but should be more convenient and more efficient.

name: merge
doc: merge(p, a, b) returns an aggregate c which merges a and b. The result is produced by examining each element x of a and y of b successively. If p(x, y) is true, then x is inserted into the result; otherwise y is inserted. If x is chosen, th e next element of a is examined, and so on. When all the elements of one aggregate are examined, the remaining elements of the other are appended. For example, merge(<, [1, 3], [2, 7, 5]) returns [1, 2, 3, 7, 5].

name: merge_unique
doc: merge_unique(p, a, b) returns an aggregate c which merges a and b uniquely. p is a binary predicate and aggregates a and b are assumed to be ordered under p and without duplicates. The result aggregate c is also ordered under p, and contain s all elements from a and b, also without duplicates. For example, merge_unique(<, [1, 3, 5], [3, 5, 6]) returns [1, 3, 5, 6].

name: jlApply
doc:
jlApply(func, obj) applies the function func with obj as parameter and returns the result as a FriCAS JLObject. For exam ple, using JLMatrix(JLObjFloat64): 

**Examples**:
```fricas
M:=nrand(4,4);
jlApply("svd", M::JLMatrix(JLObjFloat64)).S shou ld be "equivalent" to svdvals(M).
```

name: jlApply
doc:
jlApply(func, obj) applies the function func with obj as parameter and returns the result as a FriCAS JLObject. For exam ple, using JLMatrix(JLObjFloat64): 

**Examples**:

```fricas
M:=nrand(4,4);
jlApply("svd", M::JLMatrix(JLObjFloat64)).S shou ld be "equivalent" to svdvals(M).
```

name: leadingCoefficient

name: NMUnivariatePolynomial
doc:
Univariate polynomial domain using the Nemo Julia package Author: G. Vanuxem Date Created: March, 2024 Nested polynomial s Fatemans's benchmark: 

**Examples**:
```fricas
R:=NUP(NINT,'x)
x:=x::R
RR := NUP(R,'y)
y:=y::RR
RRR := NUP(RR,'z)
z:=z::RRR
T:=NUP(RRR,'t)
t:=t::T
f := 1 + x + y + z + t
p := f^30;
)set message time on
p*(p + 1);
```
p * q is the product of p with a rational number q (Fraction(Integer))
q * p is the product of p with a rational number q (Fraction(Integer))
p * n is the product of p with a non negative integer.
p * n is the product of p with a positive integer.
p * q is the sum of p and a rational number q (Fraction(Integer))
q * p is the sum of p and a rational number q (Fraction(Integer))
0 is a distinguished element, in AbelianMonoid it is the additive identity element, in MagmaWithZero it is multiplicativ e zero.
1 returns the unit element, denoted by 1.

name: antiCommutator

name: associates?
signature: (%, %) -> Boolean if % has ATVCWC and R has INTDOM or R has ENTIRER
doc: associates?(x, y) tests whether x and y are associates, i.e. differ by a unit factor.

name: associator
doc: associator(a, b, c) returns (a*b)*c-a*(b*c).

name: binomThmExpt
doc: binomThmExpt(p, q, n) returns (p+q)^n by means of the binomial theorem trick.

name: characteristic
doc: characteristic() returns the characteristic of the ring.

name: charthRoot
signature: % -> Union(%,"failed") if % has CHARNZ and R has PFECAT
doc: charthRoot(r) returns the p-th root of r, or "failed" if none exists in the domain.

name: coefficient
doc: coefficient(p, v, n) views the polynomial p as a univariate polynomial in v and returns the coefficient of the v^n term.

name: coefficient
doc: coefficient(p, lv, ln) views the polynomial p as a polynomial in the variables of lv and returns the coefficient of the term lv^ln, i.e. prod(lv_i ^ ln_i).

name: coefficient
doc: coefficient(p, e) extracts the coefficient of the monomial with exponent e from polynomial p, or returns zero if exponen t is not present.

name: coefficient
doc: coefficient(x, s) returns the coefficient of the basis element s

name: coefficients
doc: coefficients(p, seg) returns the coefficients from the exponent range seg.

name: coefficients
doc: coefficients(x) returns the list of coefficients of x.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(x) converts the variable x to a Nemo univariate polynomial.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(r) maps the ring element r to a member of the algebra.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(a) transforms a into an element of %.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(n) coerces the integer n to an element of the ring.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(s) converts the string s to a symbol.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(a) transforms a into an element of S.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(obj) coerces obj to JLObject. Convenience function.

name: commutator
doc: commutator(a, b) returns a*b-b*a.

name: composite
doc: composite(p, q) returns h if p = h(q), and "failed" if no such h exists.

name: composite
doc: composite(f, q) returns h if f = h(q), and "failed" if no such h exists.

name: conditionP
signature: Matrix(%) -> Union(Vector(%),"failed") if % has CHARNZ and R has PFECAT
doc: conditionP(m) returns a vector of elements, not all zero, whose p-th powers (p is the characteristic of the domain) are a solution of the homogeneous linear system represented by m, or "failed" is there is no such vector.

name: constantCoefficient
doc: constantCoefficient(p) returns the constant of p.

name: construct
doc: construct(l) takes a list of terms and creates the object with these components. First components of elements of l shoul d be different.

name: constructOrdered
signature: List(Record(k: NonNegativeInteger,c: R)) -> % if NonNegativeInteger has COMPAR
doc: constructOrdered(l) takes a list of terms and creates the object with these components. The list is assumed to be sorted (in reverse order) with respect to the ordering of S. If A is a monoid, then the list is assumed to contain no zero ele ments. Caution: No checking is performed, so this should only be used in cases where those conditions are assured. If in doubt use construct.

name: content
doc: content(p, v) is the gcd of the coefficients of the polynomial p when p is viewed as a univariate polynomial with respec t to the variable v. Thus, for polynomial 7*x^2*y + 14*x*y^2, the gcd of the coefficients with respect to x is 7*y.

name: content
doc: content(p) gives the gcd of the coefficients of polynomial p.

name: convert
doc: convert(a) transforms a into an element of S.

name: degree
doc: degree(p) returns the maximum of the exponents of the terms of p.

name: degree
doc: degree(p, lv) gives the list of degrees of polynomial p with respect to each of the variables in the list lv.

name: degree
doc: degree(p, v) gives the degree of polynomial p with respect to the variable v.

name: differentiate
doc: differentiate(x) returns the derivative of x. This function is a simple differential operator where no variable needs to be specified.

name: differentiate
doc: differentiate(x, v) computes the partial derivative of x with respect to v.

name: differentiate
doc: differentiate(x, s, n) computes multiple partial derivatives, i.e. n-th derivative of x with respect to s.

name: differentiate
doc: differentiate(x, [s1, ...sn]) computes successive partial derivatives, i.e. differentiate(...differentiate(x, s1)..., sn ).

name: differentiate
doc: differentiate(x, [s1, ..., sn], [n1, ..., nn]) computes multiple partial derivatives, i.e.

name: differentiate
doc: differentiate(x, deriv) differentiates x extending the derivation deriv on R.

name: differentiate
doc: differentiate(p, d, x') extends the R-derivation d to an extension D in R[x] where Dx is given by x', and returns Dp.

name: differentiate
doc: differentiate(x, deriv, n) differentiate x n times using a derivation which extends deriv on R.

name: differentiate
doc: differentiate(x, n) returns the n-th derivative of x.

name: discriminant
doc: discriminant(p, v) returns the discriminant of the polynomial p with respect to the variable v.

name: discriminant
doc: discriminant(p) returns the discriminant of the polynomial p.

name: divide
doc: divide(x, y) divides x by y producing a record containing a quotient and remainder, where the remainder is smaller (see sizeLess? from EuclideanDomain) than the divisor y.

name: divideExponents
doc: divideExponents(p, n) returns a new polynomial resulting from dividing all exponents of the polynomial p by the non nega tive integer n, or "failed" if some exponent is not exactly divisible by n.

name: elt
doc: elt(op, l) creates a form for application of op to list of arguments l.

name: elt
doc: elt(s, [a1, ..., an]) or s([a1, ..., an]) returns s subscripted by [a1, ..., an].

name: elt
doc: elt(u, i) (also written: u.i) returns the element of u indexed by i. Error: if i is not an index of u.

name: elt
doc: elt(a, r) evaluates the fraction of univariate polynomials a with the distinguished variable replaced by the constant r.

name: elt
doc: elt(a, b) evaluates the fraction of univariate polynomials a with the distinguished variable replaced by b.

name: equal?
doc: equal?(x,y) checks whether or not x and y are equal.

name: euclideanSize
doc: euclideanSize(x) returns the euclidean size of the element x. Error: if x is zero.

name: eval
doc: eval(f, x, v) replaces x by v in f.

name: eval
doc: eval(f, x = v) replaces x by v in f.

name: eval
doc: eval(f, [x1, ..., xn], [v1, ..., vn]) replaces xi by vi in f.

name: eval
doc: eval(f, [x1 = v1, ..., xn = vn]) replaces xi by vi in f.

name: exact?
doc: exact?(x) checks whether or not x is exact.

name: exactDivide
doc: exactDivide(x,y) returns the exact division of x by y. Throws a Julia error if it is not an exact division.

name: expressIdealMember
doc: expressIdealMember([f1, ..., fn], h) returns a representation of h as a linear combination of the fi or "failed" if h is not in the ideal generated by the fi.

name: exquo
doc: exquo(f, g) creates the equivalent infix form.

name: exquo
doc: exquo(a, b) either returns an element c such that c*b=a or "failed" if no such element can be found.

name: exquo
doc: exquo(p,r) returns the exact quotient of polynomial p by r, or "failed" if none exists.

name: extendedEuclidean
doc: extendedEuclidean(x, y) returns a record rec where rec.coef1*x+rec.coef2*y = rec.generator and rec.generator is a gcd of x and y. The gcd is unique only up to associates if canonicalUnitNormal is not asserted. principalIdeal provides a vers ion of this operation which accepts an arbitrary length list of arguments.

name: extendedEuclidean
doc: extendedEuclidean(x, y, z) either returns a record rec where rec.coef1*x+rec.coef2*y=z or returns "failed" if z cannot b e expressed as a linear combination of x and y.

name: factor
doc: factor(p) returns the factorization of p using the NMFactored domain.

name: factor
doc: factor(x) returns the factorization of x into irreducibles.

name: factorPolynomial
signature: SparseUnivariatePolynomial(%) -> Factored(SparseUnivariatePolynomial(%)) if R has PFECAT
doc: factorPolynomial(p) returns the factorization into irreducibles of the univariate polynomial p.

name: factorSquareFreePolynomial
signature: SparseUnivariatePolynomial(%) -> Factored(SparseUnivariatePolynomial(%)) if R has PFECAT
doc: factorSquareFreePolynomial(p) factors the univariate polynomial p into irreducibles where p is known to be square free a nd primitive with respect to its main variable.

name: fmecg
signature: (%, NonNegativeInteger, R, %) -> % if R has RING
doc: fmecg(p1, e, r, p2) returns p1 - monomial(r, e) * p2.

name: gcd
doc: gcd(x, y) returns the greatest common divisor of x and y.

name: gcd
doc: gcd(l) returns the common gcd of the elements in the list l.

name: gcdPolynomial
signature: (SparseUnivariatePolynomial(%), SparseUnivariatePolynomial(%)) -> SparseUnivariatePolynomial(%) if R has GCDDOM
doc: gcdPolynomial(p, q) returns the greatest common divisor (gcd) of univariate polynomials over the domain

name: ground
doc: ground(p) retracts polynomial p to the coefficient ring.

name: ground?
doc: ground?(p) tests if polynomial p is a member of the coefficient ring.

name: hash
signature: % -> SingleInteger if R has HASHABL and SingletonAsOrderedSet has HASHABL
doc: hash(s) calculates a hash code for s.

name: hashUpdate!
signature: (HashState, %) -> HashState if R has HASHABL and SingletonAsOrderedSet has HASHABL
doc: hashUpdate!(hs, s) computes new HashState from old and s used for incremental computation of hash values. hashUpdate! mi ght destructively work on its first argument.

name: init
doc: init() chooses an initial object for stepping.

name: integrate
doc: integrate(p) integrates the univariate polynomial p with respect to its distinguished variable.

name: irreducible?
doc: irreducible?(x) checks whether or not x is irreducible.

name: isExpt
signature: % -> Union(Record(var: SingletonAsOrderedSet,exponent: NonNegativeInteger),"failed") if R has SRING
doc: isExpt(p) returns [x, n] if polynomial p has the form x^n and n > 0.

name: isPlus
doc: isPlus(p) returns [m1, ..., mn] if polynomial p = m1 + ... + mn and n >= 2 and each mi is a nonzero monomial.

name: isTimes
doc: isTimes(p) returns [a1, ..., an] if polynomial p = a1 ... an and n >= 2, and, for each i, ai is either a nontrivial cons tant in R or else of the form x^e, where e > 0 is an integer and x is a member of VarSet.

name: jlAbout
doc: jlAbout(obj) displays Julia information about obj if you have About.jl installed in Julia. In the Julia interpreter, ent er in the package management mode with ']', and issue: pkg> add "https://github.com/tecosaur/About.jl"

name: jlApply
doc:
jlApply(func, obj) applies the function func with obj as parameter and returns the result as a FriCAS JLObject. For exam ple, using JLMatrix(JLObjFloat64): 

**Examples**:
```fricas
M:=nrand(4,4);
jlApply("svd", M::JLMatrix(JLObjFloat64)).S shou ld be "equivalent" to svdvals(M).
```

name: jlApply
doc:
jlApply(func, obj1, obj2) applies the function func with obj1 and obj2 as parameters and returns the result as a FriCAS JLObject. For example (equivalent to map(cos, v)): 

**Examples**:
```fricas
v:=urand01(5)$JLVector(JLFloat)
jlApply("map", " cos", coerce v)
```

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, obj1, obj2, obj3) applies the function func with obj1, obj2 and obj3 as parameters and returns the result as a FriCAS JLObject.

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, obj1, obj2, obj3, obj4) applies the function func with obj1, obj2, obj3 and obj4 as parameters and returns the result as a FriCAS JLObject.

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, obj1, obj2, obj3, obj4, obj5) applies the function func with obj1, obj2, obj3, obj4 and obj5 as parameters and returns the result as a FriCAS JLObject.

name: jlDisplay
doc: jlDisplay(v) pretty prints v (à la Julia).

name: jlDump
doc: jlDump(obj) dumps (shows) the Julia object (internal structure with type).

name: jlFieldNames
doc: jlFieldNames(obj) returns the field names of obj.

name: jlGetField
doc: jlGetField(obj, sym) returns the property/element sym of obj.

name: jlGetJuliaIndex
doc: jlGetJuliaIndex(obj) returns the Julia indexed dictionary index referencing the object obj. Convenience function for use in the interpreter.

name: jlGetProperty
doc: jlGetProperty(obj, sym) returns the property/element sym of obj.

name: jlId
doc: jlId(obj) returns the Julia indexed dictionary index referencing the object obj.

name: jlNMRing
doc:
jlNMRing(x) returns the FriCAS Nemo ring type of x used in Julia. For example: 

**Example**:
```fricas
jlNMRing()$NMPadicInteger(17)
```

name: jlObject
doc:
jlObject() returns the internal Julia name of the Julia module used. For example: 

**Example**:
```fricas
jlObject()$NMUnivariatePolyn omial(NINT,'x)
```

name: jlPropertyNames
doc: jlPropertyNames(obj) returns the property/element names of obj.

name: jlRef
doc: jlRef(obj) returns the internal Lisp representation of the Julia object obj.

name: jlRef
doc: jlref(str) evaluates the Julia command str and returns the corresponding FriCAS Julia mutable object.

name: jlText
doc:
jlText(obj, mimest) returns the text representation of obj as a list of String lines with mime subtype mimest, for examp le "plain" for "text/plain" or "html" for "text/html" if is implemented at Julia level. Use internally the 'show' method . For example: 

**Examples**:
```fricas
df:=jdframe nrand(6,3)
jlText(df, "plain")
jlText(df, "html")
jlText(df, "csv")
jlText(df, "latex")
```

name: jlType
doc: jlType(obj) returns the Julia type of obj.

name: jlimref
doc: jlimref(str) evaluates the Julia command str and returns the corresponding FriCAS Julia immutable object wrapped in a Ju lia RefValueAny

name: jlref
doc: jlRef(obj) returns the internal Lisp representation of the Julia object obj.

name: jlref
doc: jlref(str) evaluates the Julia command str and returns the corresponding FriCAS Julia mutable object.

name: jnulp
doc: jnulp(p) converts the univariate polynomial p to a Nemo univariate polynomial.

name: karatsubaDivide
signature: (%, NonNegativeInteger) -> Record(quotient: %,remainder: %) if R has RING
doc: karatsubaDivide(p, n) returns the same as monicDivide(p, monomial(1, n))

name: latex
doc: latex(s) returns a LaTeX-printable output representation of s.

name: lcm
doc: lcm(x, y) returns the least common multiple of x and y.

name: lcm
doc: lcm(l) returns the least common multiple of the elements of the list l.

name: lcmCoef
doc: lcmCoef(c1, c2) computes (llcm_res, coeff1, coeff2) such that llcm_res is least left common multiple of c1 and c2 and ll cm_res = coeff1*c1 = coeff2*c2

name: leadingCoefficient
doc: leadingCoefficient(z) returns the coefficient of the leading (with respect to the ordering on the indexing set) monomial of z. Error: if z has no support.

name: leadingMonomial
doc: leadingMonomial(x) returns the monomial supported by the first element from S. Error: if x has no support.

name: leadingSupport
doc: leadingSupport(z) returns the index of leading (with respect to the ordering on the indexing set) monomial of z. Error: if z has no support.

name: leadingTerm
signature: % -> Record(k: NonNegativeInteger,c: R) if NonNegativeInteger has COMPAR
doc: leadingTerm(z) returns the leading (with respect to the ordering on the indexing set) term of z. Error: if z has no supp ort.

name: leftPower
doc: leftPower(a, n) returns the n-th left power of a, i.e. leftPower(a, n) := a * leftPower(a, n-1) and leftPower(a, 0) := 1 .

name: leftPower
doc: leftPower(a, n) returns the n-th left power of a, i.e. leftPower(a, n) := a * leftPower(a, n-1) and leftPower(a, 1) := a .

name: leftRecip
doc: leftRecip(a) returns an element, which is a left inverse of a, or "failed" if such an element doesn't exist or cannot be determined (see unitsKnown).

name: linearExtend
signature: ((NonNegativeInteger -> R), %) -> R if R has COMRING
doc: linearExtend(f, x) returns the linear extension of a map defined on the basis applied to a linear combination

name: listOfTerms
doc: listOfTerms(x) returns a list lt of terms with type Record(k: S, c: R) such that x equals construct(lt). If S has Compar able then x equals constructOrdered(lt).

name: mainVariable
doc: mainVariable(p) returns the biggest variable which actually occurs in the polynomial p, or "failed" if no variables are present. fails precisely if polynomial satisfies ground?

name: makeSUP
doc: makeSUP(p) converts the polynomial p to be of type SparseUnivariatePolynomial over the same coefficients.

name: map
doc: map(f, z) returns the new element created by applying the function f to each component of the direct product element z.

name: mapExponents
doc: mapExponents(fn, u) maps function fn onto the exponents of the non-zero monomials of polynomial u.

name: minimumDegree
doc: minimumDegree(p) returns the minimal exponent of p.

name: minimumDegree
doc: minimumDegree(p) gives the least exponent of a non-zero term of polynomial p. Error: if applied to 0.

name: minimumDegree
doc: minimumDegree(p, lv) gives the list of minimum degrees of the polynomial p with respect to each of the variables in the list lv

name: minimumDegree
doc: minimumDegree(p, v) gives the minimum degree of polynomial p with respect to v, i.e. viewed a univariate polynomial in v

name: missing?
doc: missing?(obj) checks whether or not obj is missing.

name: monicDivide
doc: monicDivide(p, q) divide the polynomial p by the monic polynomial q, returning the pair [quotient, remainder]. Error: if q isn't monic.

name: monicDivide
doc: monicDivide(a, b, v) divides the polynomial a by the polynomial b, with each viewed as a univariate polynomial in v retu rning both the quotient and remainder. Error: if b is not monic with respect to v.

name: monomial
doc: monomial(a, x, n) creates the monomial a*x^n where a is a polynomial, x is a variable and n is a nonnegative integer.

name: monomial
doc: monomial(a, [v1..vn], [e1..en]) returns a*prod(vi^ei).

name: monomial
doc: monomial(a, s) constructs a direct product element with the s component set to a

name: monomial?
doc: monomial?(p) checks whether or not p is a monomial.

name: monomialRecursive?
doc: monomialRecursive?(p) checks whether or not p is monomial recursively (all scalar types).

name: monomials
doc: monomials(x) returns the list of r_i*b_i whose sum is x.

name: mullow
doc: mullow(p1,p2,n) is the truncated multiplication of p1 and p2 by n.

name: multiEuclidean
doc: multiEuclidean([f1, ..., fn], z) returns a list of coefficients [a1, ..., an] such that  z / prod fi = sum aj/fj. If no such list of coefficients exists, "failed" is returned.

name: multiplyExponents
doc: multiplyExponents(p, n) returns a new polynomial resulting from multiplying all exponents of the polynomial p by the non negative integer n.

name: multivariate
doc: multivariate(sup, v) converts an anonymous univariable polynomial sup to a polynomial in the variable v.

name: mutable?
doc: mutable?(obj) checks whether or not obj is mutable.

name: nemoULPPrint
doc: nemoULPPrint(bool) set the output mode. If set to false, use the FriCAS output mode if possible. Otherwise use the Nemo one (default).

name: nextItem
doc: nextItem(x) returns the next item, or "failed" if domain is exhausted.

name: nothing?
doc: nothing?(obj) checks whether or not obj is nothing.

name: numberOfMonomials
doc: numberOfMonomials(x) returns the number of monomials of x.

name: one?
doc: one?(a) tests whether a is the unit 1.

name: opposite?
doc: opposite?(x,y) holds if the sum of x and y is 0.

name: order
doc: order(p, q) returns the largest n such that q^n divides polynomial p i.e. the order of p(x) at q(x)=0.

name: patternMatch
signature: (%, Pattern(Float), PatternMatchResult(Float,%)) -> PatternMatchResult(Float,%) if R has PATMAB(FLOAT) and R has RING and SingletonAsOrderedSet has PATMAB(FLOAT)

name: patternMatch
signature: (%, Pattern(Integer), PatternMatchResult(Integer,%)) -> PatternMatchResult(Integer,%) if R has PATMAB(INT) and R has RING and SingletonAsOrderedSet has PATMAB(INT)

name: plenaryPower
doc: plenaryPower(a, n) is recursively defined to be plenaryPower(a, n-1)*plenaryPower(a, n-1) for n>1 and a for n=1.

name: pomopo!
doc: pomopo!(p1, r, e, p2) returns p1 + monomial(r, e) * p2 and may use p1 as workspace. The constant r is assumed to be nonz ero.

name: prime?
doc: prime?(x) tests if x can never be written as the product of two non-units of the ring, i.e. x is an irreducible element.

name: primitiveMonomials
doc: primitiveMonomials(p) gives the list of monomials of the polynomial p with their coefficients removed. Note: primitiveMo nomials(sum(a_(i) X^(i))) = [X^(1), ..., X^(n)].

name: primitivePart
doc: primitivePart(p) returns the unit normalized form of polynomial p divided by the content of p.

name: primitivePart
doc: primitivePart(p, v) returns the unitCanonical associate of the polynomial p with its content with respect to the variabl e v divided out.

name: principalIdeal
signature: List(%) -> Record(coef: List(%),generator: %) if R has FIELD
doc: principalIdeal([f1, ..., fn]) returns a record whose generator component is a generator of the ideal generated by [f1, . .., fn] whose coef component satisfies generator = sum (input.i * coef.i)

name: pseudoDivide
signature: (%, %) -> Record(coef: R,quotient: %,remainder: %) if R has INTDOM
doc: pseudoDivide(p, q) returns [c, s, r], when p' := p*lc(q)^(deg p - deg q + 1) = c * p is pseudo right-divided by q, i.e. p' = s q + r.

name: pseudoQuotient
doc: pseudoQuotient(p, q) returns s, the quotient when p' := p*lc(q)^(deg p - deg q + 1) is pseudo right-divided by q, i.e. p ' = s q + r.

name: pseudoRemainder
doc: pseudoRemainder(p, q) = r, for polynomials p and q, returns the remainder r when p' := p*lc(q)^(deg p - deg q + 1) is ps eudo right-divided by q, i.e. p' = s q + r.

name: quo
doc: x quo y is the same as divide(x, y).quotient. See divide from EuclideanDomain.

name: recip
doc: recip(a) returns an element, which is both a left and a right inverse of a, or "failed" if such an element doesn't exist or cannot be determined (see unitsKnown).

name: reducedSystem
doc: reducedSystem(A) returns a matrix B such that A x = 0 and B x = 0 have the same solutions in R.

name: reducedSystem
doc: reducedSystem(A, v) returns a matrix B and a vector w such that A x = v and B x = w have the same solutions in R.

name: reductum
doc: reductum(z) returns a new element created by removing the leading coefficient/support pair from the element z. Error: if z has no support.

name: rem
doc: x rem y is the same as divide(x, y).remainder. See divide from EuclideanDomain.

name: resultant
doc: resultant(p, q, v) returns the resultant of the polynomials p and q with respect to the variable v.

name: resultant
doc: resultant(p, q) returns the resultant of the polynomials p and q.

name: retract
doc: retract(a) transforms a into an element of S if possible. Error: if a cannot be made into an element of S.

name: retractIfCan
doc: retractIfCan(a) transforms a into an element of S if possible. Returns "failed" if a cannot be made into an element of S .

name: reverse
doc: reverse the coefficients of p (the leading becomes the trailing) and normalise the resulting polynomial.

name: reverse
doc: reverse the coefficients of p (the leading becomes the trailing) and normalise the resulting polynomial. Adjust the length to n so the resulting polynomial is truncated or padded with zeroes before the leading term if necessary

name: reverse
doc: reverse the coefficients of p (the leading becomes the trailing) and normalise the resulting polynomial. Adjust the leng th to n so the resulting polynomial is truncated or padded with zeroes before the leading term if necessary

name: rightPower
doc: rightPower(a, n) returns the n-th right power of a, i.e. rightPower(a, n) := rightPower(a, n-1) * a and rightPower(a, 0) := 1.

name: rightPower
doc: rightPower(a, n) returns the n-th right power of a, i.e. rightPower(a, n) := rightPower(a, n-1) * a and rightPower(a, 1) := a.

name: rightRecip
doc: rightRecip(a) returns an element, which is a right inverse of a, or "failed" if such an element doesn't exist or cannot be determined (see unitsKnown).

name: sample
doc: sample yields a value of type %

name: separate
doc: separate(p, q) returns [a, b] such that p = a b, a is relatively prime to q and b divides some power of q.

name: shiftLeft
doc: shiftLeft(p, n) returns p * monomial(1, n)

name: shiftRight
doc: shiftRight(p, n) returns monicDivide(p, monomial(1, n)).quotient

name: sizeLess?
doc: sizeLess?(x, y) tests whether x is strictly smaller than y with respect to the euclideanSize from EuclideanDomain. Note: zero is considered smaller than every nonzero element.

name: smaller?
signature: (%, %) -> Boolean if R has COMPAR and NonNegativeInteger has COMPAR or R has COMPARR
doc: smaller?(x, y) is a strict ordering on depending on representatives of elements of the set. If % has Comparable then sma ller? gives mathematical linear order.

name: solveLinearPolynomialEquation
doc: solveLinearPolynomialEquation([f1, ..., fn], g) (where the fi are relatively prime to each other) returns a list of ai s uch that g/prod fi = sum ai/fi or returns "failed" if no such list of ai's exists. (%)),"failed")

name: squareFree
doc: squareFree(p) returns the square free factorization of the polynomial p.

name: squareFreePart
doc: squareFreePart(p) returns product of all the irreducible factors of polynomial p each taken with multiplicity one.

name: squareFreePolynomial
signature: SparseUnivariatePolynomial(%) -> Factored(SparseUnivariatePolynomial(%)) if R has PFECAT
doc: squareFreePolynomial(p) returns the square-free factorization of the univariate polynomial p.

name: string
doc: string(jt) returns the string representation of jt.

name: subResultantGcd
doc: subResultantGcd(p, q) computes the gcd of the polynomials p and q using the SubResultant GCD algorithm.

name: subtractIfCan
doc: subtractIfCan(x, y) returns an element z such that z+y=x or "failed" if no such element exists.

name: support
doc: support(x) returns the list of basis elements with nonzero coefficients.

The coefficient ring may be non-commutative, but the variables are assume d to commute. The monomial ordering used for internal storage can be one of :lex, :deglex or :degrevlex. p * q is the product of p with a rational number q (Fraction(Integer))
q * p is the product of p with a rational q (Fraction(Integer))
* is the positive integer multiplication.
* is the non negative integer multiplication.
p + q is the sum of a p with a rational number q (Fraction(Integer))
q + p is the sum of a p with a rational number q (Fraction(Integer))
0 returns the input form corresponding to 0.
1 returns the input form corresponding to 1.

name: jlMPFRApply
doc: jlMPFRApply(func, x) applies the function pointer func to x. It is expected that the C function modifies the first parameters for the returned value (provided by FriCAS and returned here) and and as a last parameter, the rounding mode. See MPFR. Uses Julia rounding mode, default to nearest. \example{mpfr:=jlDlOpen "libmpfr"} \example{sym:= jlDlSym(mpfr,jsym(mpfr_gamma))} \example{val:=jfloat("0.7");} \example{jlMPFRApply(sym,val)} => 1.29805533264755778568117117915281161778... \example{jlDlClose(mpfr)}

Uses Julia rounding mode, default to nearest. \example{mpfr:=j lDlOpen "libmpfr"} \example{sym:= jlDlSym(mpfr,jsym(mpfr_pow))} \example{val:=jfloat("0.7");} \example{jlMPFRApply(sym,val, jfloat(2))} \example{jlDlClose(mpfr)}

name: jlMPFRApply

It is expected that the C function modifies the first parameters for the returned value (provided by FriCAS and returned here) and as a last parameter, the rounding mode (the default mode is used here). See MPFR. Uses Julia rounding mode, default to nearest. \example{mpfr:=j lDlOpen "libmpfr"} \example{sym:= jlDlSym(mpfr,jsym(mpfr_fma))} \example{val:=jfloat("0.7");} \example{jlMPFRApply(sym,val, jfloat(2), jfloat(5))} \example{jlDlClose(mpfr)}

name: merge
doc: merge(p, a, b) returns an aggregate c which merges a and b. The result is produced by examining each element x of a and y of b successively. If p(x, y) is true, then x is inserted into the result; otherwise y is inserted. If x is chosen, th e next element of a is examined, and so on. When all the elements of one aggregate are examined, the remaining elements of the other are appended. For example, merge(<, [1, 3], [2, 7, 5]) returns [1, 2, 3, 7, 5].

name: merge_unique
signature: (((R, R) -> Boolean), %, %) -> % if % has ATFINAG and R has BASTYPE
doc: merge_unique(p, a, b) returns an aggregate c which merges a and b uniquely. p is a binary predicate and aggregates a and b are assumed to be ordered under p and without duplicates. The result aggregate c is also ordered under p, and contain s all elements from a and b, also without duplicates. For example, merge_unique(<, [1, 3, 5], [3, 5, 6]) returns [1, 3, 5, 6].

name: reduce

name: reduce

jlPlotTitle!(title) draws `title' as plot title in the current plot. For example: jlPlotTitle! "sin(x)" if you have the LaTeXStrings Julia package 

**Examples**:
```fricas
jlPlotTitle! jlLatex latex sin(x) For simple expressions title will automatically be enclosed between $. So use:
jlPlotTitle! jlLatex "sin(x)" For normal text and equations insert dollar sign s $ as needed.
jlPlotTitle! jlLatex "Plot: $sin(x)$"
```

name: QQ
doc: QQ(q) returns q as a Nemo rational. Convenience function.

name: ZZ
doc: ZZ(i) returns i as a Nemo integer. Convenience function.

name: jlAddPackage
doc: jlAddPackage(package) adds package to Julia. For example, jlAddPackage("PyCall") will add the PyCall package.

name: jlBuildPackage
doc: jlBuildPackage(package) builds package in Julia. For example, jlBuildPackage("PyCall") will build the PyCall package.

name: jlDefined?
doc: jlDefined?(sym) checks whether or not sym is defined in Julia.

name: jlDefined?
doc: jlDefined?(str) checks whether or not str is defined in Julia. For example: jlDefined?("sin") will check if sin is defined.

name: jlEvalString
doc: jlEvalString(str) evaluates str in Julia with no output.

name: jlEvalString
doc: jlEvalString(str) evaluates str in Julia, where the output is a Boolean.

name: jlEvalString
doc: jlEvalString(str) evaluates str in Julia, where the output is a JLInt64.

name: jlEvalString
doc: jlEvalString(str) evaluates str in Julia, where the output is an Integer.

name: jlEvalString
doc: jlEvalString(str) evaluates str in Julia, where the output is a NonNegativeInteger.

name: jlEvalString
doc: jlEvalString(str) evaluates str in Julia, where the output is a PositiveInteger.

name: jlEvalString
doc: jlEvalString(str) evaluates str in Julia, where the output is a String.

name: jlEvalString
doc: jlEvalString(str) evaluates str in Julia, where the output is a JLFloat32.

name: jlEvalString
doc: jlEvalString(str) evaluates str in Julia, where the output is a JLFloat64.

name: jlGCCollect
doc: jlGCCollect() forces a Julia garbage collector run.

name: jlGCPackages
doc: jlGCPackages() forces a Julia garbage collector run on all installed packages.

name: jlImport
doc: jlImport(modpackfunc) imports the module, package or function modpackfunc and makes it available. Returns false if it cannot be imported.

name: jlInclude
doc: jlInclude(file.jl) loads and evaluates the content of the Julia file file.jl in the current global scope.

name: jlInitialize
doc: jlInitialize(init) initializes the Julia environment if init is true, otherwise clears the Julia environment. Normally, it should not be used since it is automatically called.

name: jlListPackages
doc: jlListPackages() displays the status of all installed packages in Julia.

name: jlRandomString
doc: jlRandomString(n) returns a random string of n characters.

name: jlRemovePackage
doc: jlRemovePackage(package) removes package from Julia. For example, jlRemovePackage("PyCall") will remove the PyCall package.

name: jlSeed!
doc: jlSeed!(n) reseeds the Julia random number generator if applicable (Some random number generators don't accept a seed).

name: jlTestPackage
doc: jlTestPackage(package) tests package in Julia. For example, jlTestPackage("PyCall") will test the PyCall package.

name: jlUpdateAllPackages
doc: jlUpdateAllPackages() updates all packages in Julia.

name: jlUpdatePackage
doc: jlUpdatePackage(package) updates package in Julia. For example, jlUpdatePackage("PyCall") will update the PyCall package.

name: jlUsing
doc: jlUsing(modpack) loads the module or package modpack and makes its exported names available. Returns false if it cannot be loaded.

name: JLStringUtilities

name: jlLatex
doc: jlLatex(str) returns the String corresponding to a Julia LaTeX expression, that is, "L"str"" if your Julia installation supports it (LaTeXStrings package). Convenience function.

name: jlMessageStyled
doc: jlMessageStyled(message) prints the message with formatted style within braces (I am {red:here}). For example: \example{jlMessageStyled("{red:■} {green:■} {yellow:■} {blue:■} {magenta:■} {cyan:■}")}

name: jlMessageStyled
doc: jlMessageStyled(message, color) prints the message with formatted `color` (english color). For example: \example{jlMessageStyled("I AM HERE!!!", "red")}

name: jlRegex
doc: jlRegex(str) returns the String corresponding to a Julia regular expression, that is, "r_"str_"". Convenience function.

name: jlRegexMatch?

name: jlRegexReplace
doc: jlRegexReplace(str, regex, subst) will replace captured regular expressions in str with subst. More information in String documentation of Julia. For example: jlRegexReplace("hey", jlRegex("$"), jlSubstitute(" you!"))

name: jlSplit
doc: jlSplit(str, delims, n) splits str with delimiter(s) delims (a string or a regular expression). Returns a list of size n. Parses entirely str if n = 0.

name: jlSplit

name: jlSubstitute

name: jlToLatex
doc: jlToLatex(str) converts the string str to LaTeX for supported expressions. The Julia package Latexify needs to be installed. jlToLatex("sin(sqrt(2))") => "$\sin\left( \sqrt{2} \right)$"

name: jdlink
doc: jdlink(lib) opens/loads the dynamic shared library lib and returns a reference pointer that can be used to obtain addresses of its exported symbols using jlDlSym. It is up to the user to unload the shared object when it is no longer necessary using jlDlClose. \example{libm := jdlink "libopenlibm"} Throws a Julia error if it is not found. Use jlDlOpen for a version with options and/or without Julia errors.

name: jlDlCApply
doc: jlDlCApply(func,x) applies the function pointer func to x. The Julia type of x must be compatible with the Libdl Julia module. Type of the returned value is assumed to be the same as the type of x. For example: \example{libm:= jlDlOpen "libopenlibm"} \example{squareRoot:=jlDlSym(libm,jsym(sqrt))} \example{jlDlCApply(squareRoot,jobject("2."))}

name: jlDlCApply
doc: jlDlCApply(func, ctype, x, xctype) applies the function pointer func to x given its Julia C type (xctype) or its supported Julia type, for example "Float64" or "Cdouble". Returned value is assumed to be a C type ctype (or any Julia supported types). For example: \example{libm:= jlDlOpen "libopenlibm"} \example{squareRoot:= jlDlSym(libm,jsym(sqrt))} \example{jlDlCApply(squareRoot, "Cdouble", jobject("2."), "Cdouble")} \example{sinus:=jlDlSym(libm,jsym(sin))} \example{jlDlCApply(sinus,"Float64", jobject("2."), "Float64")}

name: jlDlCApply

name: jlDlOpen
doc: jlDlOpen(lib) opens/loads the dynamic shared library lib and returns a reference pointer that can be used to obtain addresses of its exported symbols using jlDlSym. It is up to the user to unload the shared object when it is no longer used. Does not throw an error if the library cannot be loaded and returns 'nothing' in this case. Use the nothing? operation on the returned value if necessary.

name: jlDlOpen
doc: jlDlOpen(lib, flags) opens/loads the dynamic shared library lib and returns a reference pointer that can be used to obtain addresses of its exported symbols using jlDlSym. It is up to the user to unload the shared object when it is no longer used. Does not throw an error if the library cannot be loaded by default and returns nothing in this case. Use the nothing? operation on the returned value if necessary. The Julia module Libdl must be loaded/imported before using this function. \example{jlUsing "Libdl"} -- for flags \example{jlDlOpen("libopenlibm", jobject "Libdl.RTLD_NOW")} flags can be one or combination of: RTLD_DEEPBIND RTLD_FIRST RTLD_GLOBAL RTLD_LAZY RTLD_LOCAL RTLD_NODELETE RTLD_NOLOAD RTLD_NOW Note: the Julia module Libdl must be loaded or imported before using these flags.

'throw' determines whether or not Julia throws an error if the library cannot be loaded. \example{jlDlOpen("libopenlibm", true)}

name: jlDlOpen

Use the nothing? operation on the returned value if necessary. 'throw' determines whether or not Julia throws an error if the library cannot be loaded. The Julia module must be be loaded/imported before using this function. \example{jlDlOpen("libopenlibm", jobject "Libdl.RTLD_NOW", false)} flags can be one or combination of: RTLD_DEEPBIND RTLD_FIRST RTLD_GLOBAL RTLD_LAZY RTLD_LOCAL RTLD_NODELETE RTLD_NOLOAD RTLD_NOW Note: the Julia module Libdl must be loaded or imported before using these flags.
