name: less?
doc: less?(u, n) tests if u has less than n elements.

name: map
doc: map(f, u) returns a copy of u with each element x replaced by f(x). For collections, map(f, u) = [f(x) for x in u].

name: map
doc: map(f, u, v) returns a new aggregate w with elements z = f(x, y) for corresponding elements x and y from u and v. Note: w.i = f(u.i, v.i).

name: map!
doc: map!(f, u) destructively replaces each element x of u by f(x).

name: max
doc: max(x,y) returns the maximum of x and y relative to "<".

name: max
doc: max(u) returns maximal element of u. Error if u is empty.

name: max
doc: max(p, u) returns maximal element of u with respect to total ordering predicate p. Error if u is empty.

name: maxIndex
doc: maxIndex(u) returns the maximum index i of aggregate u. Note: in general, maxIndex(u) = reduce(max, indices u); for List , maxIndex(u) = #u.

name: member?
signature: (E, %) -> Boolean if % has ATFINAG and E has BASTYPE
doc: member?(x, u) tests if x is a member of u. For collections, member?(x, u) = reduce(or, [x=y for y in u], false). However , member?(x, u) returns as soon as it finds a member.

name: members
doc: members(u) returns a list of the consecutive elements of u. For multisets members gives result with no repetition. See a lso parts.

name: merge
doc: merge(u, v) merges u and v in ascending order. Note: merge(u, v) = merge(<=, u, v).

name: merge
doc: merge(p, a, b) returns an aggregate c which merges a and b. The result is produced by examining each element x of a and y of b successively. If p(x, y) is true, then x is inserted into the result; otherwise y is inserted. If x is chosen, th e next element of a is examined, and so on. When all the elements of one aggregate are examined, the remaining elements of the other are appended. For example, merge(<, [1, 3], [2, 7, 5]) returns [1, 2, 3, 7, 5].

name: merge_unique
signature: (((E, E) -> Boolean), %, %) -> % if % has ATFINAG and E has BASTYPE
doc: merge_unique(p, a, b) returns an aggregate c which merges a and b uniquely. p is a binary predicate and aggregates a and b are assumed to be ordered under p and without duplicates. The result aggregate c is also ordered under p, and contain s all elements from a and b, also without duplicates. For example, merge_unique(<, [1, 3, 5], [3, 5, 6]) returns [1, 3, 5, 6].

name: min
doc: min(x,y) returns the minimum of x and y relative to "<".

name: min
doc: min(u) returns minimal element of u. Error if u is empty.

name: minIndex
doc: minIndex(u) returns the minimum index i of aggregate u. Note: in general, minIndex(a) = reduce(min, indices a); for List , minIndex(a) = 1.

name: missing?
doc: missing?(obj) checks whether or not obj is missing.

name: more?
doc: more?(u, n) tests if u has more than n elements.

name: mutable?
doc: mutable?(obj) checks whether or not obj is mutable.

name: negative?
signature: % -> Boolean if % has SETCATZ and % has ATFINAG and E has ORDSET
doc: negative?(x) tests whether x is strictly less than 0.

name: new
doc: new(n, x) returns a new aggregate of size n all of whose entries are x.

name: norm
doc: norm(v) computes the norm of the vector v.

name: nothing?
doc: nothing?(obj) checks whether or not obj is nothing.

name: numeric
doc: numeric(expr) returns numerical expr if possible.

name: numeric
doc: numeric(expr, prec) returns the numerical expr with prec digits of precision if possible.

name: numeric?
doc: numeric?(x) checks whether or not x is or would yield a number.

name: outerProduct
doc: outerProduct(u, v) constructs the matrix whose (i, j)'th element is u(i)*v(j).

name: part
doc: part(agg,i) returns the i-th element.

name: parts
doc: parts(u) returns a list of the consecutive elements of u. For finite collections, construct(parts(u)) = u.

name: position
doc: position(x, a) returns the index i of the first occurrence of x in a, and minIndex(a) - 1 if there is no such x.

name: position
doc: position(x, a, n) returns the index i of the first occurrence of x in a where i >= n, and minIndex(a) - 1 if no such x i s found.

name: position
doc: position(p, a) returns the index i of the first x in a such that p(x) is true, and minIndex(a) - 1 if there is no such x .

name: positive?
signature: % -> Boolean if % has SETCATZ and % has ATFINAG and E has ORDSET
doc: positive?(x) tests whether x is strictly greater than 0.

name: prepend
doc: prepend(l, elt) prepends elt to the list l.

name: qelt
doc: qelt(agg,i) returns the i-th element. No checks are done at the FriCAS level.

name: qelt
doc: qelt(u, x) applies u to x without checking whether x is in the domain of u. If x is not in the domain of u a memory-acce ss violation may occur. If a check on whether x is in the domain of u is required, use the function elt.

name: qsetelt
doc: qsetelt(l,i,elem) returns a copy of l with i-th element replaced by the element elem. No checks are done at the FriCAS l evel.

name: qsetelt!
doc: qsetelt!(l,i,elem) returns l with i-th element replaced by elem. No checks are done at the FriCAS level.

name: qsetelt!
doc: qsetelt!(u, x, y) sets the image of x to be y under u, without checking that x is in the domain of u. If such a check is required use the function setelt!.

name: reduce
doc: reduce(f, u) reduces the binary operation f across u. For example, if u is [x, y, ..., z] then reduce(f, u) returns f(.. f(f(x, y), ...), z). Note: if u has one element x, reduce(f, u) returns x. Error: if u is empty.

name: reduce
doc: reduce(f, u, x) reduces the binary operation f across u, where x is the identity operation of f. Same as reduce(f, u) if u has 2 or more elements. Returns f(y, x) if u has one element y. Returns x if u is empty. For example, reduce(+, u, 0) returns the sum of the elements of u.

name: reduce
doc: reduce(f, u, x, z) reduces the binary operation f across u, stopping when an "absorbing element" z is encountered. As fo r reduce(f, u, x), x is the identity element of f. Same as reduce(f, u, x) when u contains no element z. Thus the third argument x is returned when u is empty.

name: remove
doc: remove(x, u) returns a copy of u with all elements equal to x removed. Note: remove(x, u) = [y for y in u | y ~= x].

name: remove
doc: remove(p, u) returns a copy of u removing all elements x such that p(x) is true. Note: remove(p, u) = [x for x in u | no t p(x)].

name: removeDuplicates
doc: removeDuplicates(u) returns a copy of u with all duplicates removed.

name: replacePart
doc: replacePart(expr, part) replaces expr using rule(s) expressing position(s).

name: rest
doc: rest(agg) returns agg without the first element.

name: reverse
doc: reverse(a) returns a copy of a with elements in reverse order.

name: reverse
doc: reverse(agg, lev) reverses the elements of agg at level lev.

name: reverse
doc: reverse(agg, levels) reverses the elements of agg using levels.

name: reverse!
signature: % -> % if % has ATFINAG and % has ATSHMUT
doc: reverse!(u) returns u with its elements in reverse order.

name: riffle
doc: riffle(agg, elts) riffles (interleaves) element(s) elts i.e. inserts them.

name: riffle
doc: riffle(agg, elts, inds) riffles (interleaves) element(s) elts i.e. inserts them. If inds is min, max, n inserts at posit ion min, min+n, min+2n..max.

name: rightTrim
signature: (%, E) -> % if % has ATFINAG and E has BASTYPE
doc: rightTrim(u, x) returns a copy of u with all trailing occurrences of x deleted. For example, rightTrim(" abc ", char " " ) returns " abc".

name: sample
doc: sample yields a value of type %

name: select
doc: select(p, u) returns a copy of u containing only those elements such p(x) is true. Note: select(p, u) = [x for x in u | p(x)].

name: setIntersection
doc: setIntersection(agg1, agg2) is the intersection set operator.

name: setelt
doc: setelt(l,i,elem) returns a copy of l with i-th element replaced by the element elem.

name: setelt!
doc: setelt!(l,i,elem) returns l with i-th element replaced by elem.

name: setelt!
doc: setelt!(u, x, y) sets the image of x to be y under u, if x is in the domain of u. Error: if x is not in the domain of u.

name: setelt!
doc: setelt!(u, i..j, x) (also written: u(i..j) := x) destructively replaces each element in the segment u(i..j) by x. The va lue x is returned. Note: u is destructively changed so that u.k := x for k in i..j; its length remains unchanged.

name: sign
signature: % -> Integer if % has SETCATZ and % has ATFINAG and E has ORDSET
doc: sign(x) is 1 if x is positive, -1 if x is negative, 0 if x equals 0.

name: size?
doc: size?(u, n) tests if u has exactly n elements.

name: smaller?
signature: (%, %) -> Boolean if % has ATFINAG and E has COMPAR or % has ATFINAG and E has ORDSET
doc: smaller?(x, y) is a strict ordering on depending on representatives of elements of the set. If % has Comparable then sma ller? gives mathematical linear order.

name: sort
doc: sort(u) returns a copy of u with elements in ascending order. Note: sort(u) = sort(<, u).

name: sort
doc: sort(p, a) returns a copy of a sorted using total ordering predicate p.

name: sort!
doc: sort!(u) returns u with its elements in ascending order.

name: sort!
doc: sort!(p, u) returns u with its elements ordered by p.

name: sorted?
doc: sorted?(u) tests if the elements of u are in ascending order.

name: sorted?
doc: sorted?(p, a) tests if a is sorted according to predicate p.

name: string
doc: string(jt) returns the string representation of jt.

name: swap!
signature: (%, Integer, Integer) -> Void if % has ATSHMUT
doc: swap!(u, i, j) interchanges elements i and j of aggregate u. No meaningful value is returned.

name: take
doc: take(l,i) returns the first i elements.

name: toString
doc: toString(obj) returns the string representation of obj.

name: total
doc: total(agg) returns the sum of the elements in agg.

name: transpose
doc: transpose(v) transposes v. For esoteric purpose, and if you know what you are doing. There is only one type of vector in the Wolfram language. Should not be used, and for normal purpose, does nothing.

name: trim
signature: (%, E) -> % if % has ATFINAG and E has BASTYPE
doc: trim(u, x) returns a copy of u with all occurrences of x deleted from right and left ends. For example, trim(" abc ", ch ar " ") returns "abc".

name: union
doc: union(agg1, agg2) is the union set operator. Elements are sorted on output.

name: vector
doc: vector(list) returns list as a vector. Inplace coercion. \example{vector(range(5)}

name: zero
doc: zero(n) creates a zero vector of length n.

name: zero?
doc: zero?(x) returns true if x is a zero vector, false otherwise.

name: WSMatrix
doc: Julia Wolfram Symbolic matrices using the MathLink Julia package.
#(u) returns the number of elements in u.
#(agg) returns the length of agg. 0 if it is a scalar, an index for example.
a * b is the matrix multiplication, not the element-wise multiplication. WS error if dimensions are incompatible.
n*a scales the matrix a by n.
\spad{r*x} is the left scalar multiple of the scalar r and the matrix x.
\spad{x * r} is the right scalar multiple of the scalar r and the matrix x.
\spad{x * c} is the product of the matrix x and the column vector c. Error: if the dimensions are incompatible.
\spad{r * x} is the product of the row vector r and the matrix x. Error: if the dimensions are incompatible.
a + b is the matrix addition. WS error if dimensions are incompatible.

name: Pfaffian
doc: Pfaffian(m) returns the Pfaffian of the matrix m. Error: if the matrix is not antisymmetric.
a^n is the matrix power by the positive integer n.
a^n is the matrix power by the non-negative integer n.

name: accumulate
doc: accumulate(agg) returns the partial sums of elements in agg.

name: adjoint
doc: adjoint(m) returns the adjoint of m, i.e. the conjugate transposition of m.

name: adjugate
doc: adjugate(m) returns the adjugate of square m.

name: antisymmetric?
doc: \spad{antisymmetric?(m)} returns true if the matrix m is square and antisymmetric (i.e. \spad{m[i, j] = -m[j, i]} for all i and j) and false otherwise.

name: any?
doc: any?(p, u) tests if p(x) is true for any element x of u. Note: for collections, any?(p, u) = reduce(or, map(p, u), false , true). However, any?(p, u) returns as soon as it finds an element for which p gives true.

name: append
doc: append(l, elt) appends elt to the list l.

name: array2
doc: array2(ll) constructs a 2-dimensional array, the inner list being the rows.

name: blockConcat
doc: blockConcat(ll) concatenates arrays row and column wise, building an array from blocks. The order is row major as in mat rix.

name: blockSplit
doc: blockSplit(a, [n1,...,ni], [m1,...,mi]) splits a into multiple subarrays row and column wise, such that element at posit ion k, l has nk rows and ml columns. Error: if number of rows of a is different than n1 + ... + ni or number of columns of a is different than m1 + ... + mj

name: blockSplit
doc: blockSplit(a, n, m) splits a into n*m subarrays of equal size row and column wise, dividing a into blocks. Error: if num ber of rows of a is not divisible by n or number of columns of a is not divisible by m.

name: cholesky
doc: cholesky(m) computes the Cholesky decomposition of the positive definite/hermitian square matrix m.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(col) converts the column col to a column matrix.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(list) tries to coerce list to a WSAggregate.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(a) transforms a into an element of S.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(obj) coerces obj to JLObject. Convenience function.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(expr) returns the WSExpression representation of expr.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(v) coerces inplace v to a WS matrix.

name: colSlice
doc: colSlice(m) returns a segment s such that for m the access m(i, s) gives the i-th row.

name: column
doc: column(mat,i) returns the i-th column.

name: column
doc: column(m, j) returns the jth column of m error check to determine if index is in proper ranges

name: columnSpace
doc: columnSpace(m) returns a sublist of columns of the matrix m forming a basis of its column space.

name: convert
doc: convert(a) transforms a into an element of S.

name: copy
doc: copy(u) returns a top-level (non-recursive) copy of u. Note: for collections, copy(u) = [x for x in u].

name: count
doc: count(x, u) returns the number of occurrences of x in u. For collections, count(x, u) = reduce(+, [1 for y in u | x = y] , 0).

name: count
doc: count(p, u) returns the number of elements x in u such that p(x) is true. For collections, count(p, u) = reduce(+, [1 fo r x in u | p(x)], 0).

name: delete
doc: delete(l, inds) deletes element(s) of the list l at index(es) inds.

name: determinant
doc: determinant(m) returns the determinant of the matrix m. Error: if the matrix is not square.

name: diagonal
doc: diagonal(m) returns the diagonal elements of m as a vector.

name: diagonal?
doc: \spad{diagonal?(m)} returns true if the matrix m is square and diagonal (i.e. all entries of m not on the diagonal are zero) and false otherwise.

name: diagonalMatrix
doc: \spad{diagonalMatrix(l)} returns a diagonal matrix with elements of l as diagonal elements.

name: diagonalMatrix
doc: diagonalMatrix([m1, ..., mk]) creates a block diagonal matrix M with block matrices  m1, ...,  mk down the diagonal, wit h 0 block matrices elsewhere. More precisely: if ri := nrows mi, ci := ncols mi, then m is an (r1+..+rk) by (c1+..+ck) m atrix with entries m.i.j = ml.(i-r1-..-r(l-1)).(j-c1-..-c(l-1)), if (r1+..+r(l-1)) < i <= r1+..+rl and (c1+..+c(l-1)) < i <= c1+..+cl, m.i.j = 0 otherwise.

name: diagonalMatrix
doc: diagonalMatrix(l) returns a diagonal matrix with the elements of l on the diagonal.

name: differences
doc: differences(agg) returns the differences between adjacent elements in agg.

name: dimensions
doc: dimensions(agg) returns dimensions of agg.

name: eigenSystem
doc: eigenvectors(m) returns the eigenvectors of the square matrix m.

name: eigenSystem
doc: eigenSystem(m) computes the spectral decomposition of the square matrix m. It returns in a Record, the eigenvalues, sele ctor 'values', and the eigenvectors selector 'vectors'.

name: eigenvalues
doc: eigenvalues(m) returns the eigenvalues of the square matrix m.

name: eigenvectors
doc: eigenvectors(m) returns the eigenvectors of the square matrix m.

name: elt
doc: elt(mat, m, n) returns the element (m,n) of the matrix mat.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, row, colList) returns an 1-by-n array consisting of elements of x, where n = # colList. If colList = [j<1>, j<2>, ..., j<n>], then the (k, l)th entry of elt(x, row, colList) is x(row, j<l>).

name: elt
doc: elt(x, row, ls2) is equivalent to elt(x, row, l2) where l2 is obtained by appending expansions of elements of ls2, but s hould be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(op, l) creates a form for application of op to list of arguments l.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, rowList, col) returns an m-by-1 array consisting of elements of x, where m = # rowList. If rowList = [i<1>, i<2>, ..., i<m>], then the (k, l)th entry of elt(x, rowList, col) is x(i<k>, col).

name: elt
doc: elt(x, rowList, colList) returns an m-by-n array consisting of elements of x, where m = # rowList and n = # colList. If rowList = [i<1>, i<2>, ..., i<m>] and colList = [j<1>, j<2>, ..., j<n>], then the (k, l)th entry of elt(x, rowList, colL ist) is x(i<k>, j<l>).

name: elt
doc: elt(x, rowList, s) is equivalent to elt(x, rowList, expand(s)) but should be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, ls1, col) is equivalent to elt(x, l1, col) where l1 is obtained by appending expansions of elements of ls1, but s hould be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, ls1, ls2) is equivalent to elt(x, l1, l2) where li is obtained by appending expansions of elements of lsi, but sh ould be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, ls1, s2) is equivalent to elt(x, l1, l2) where li is obtained by appending expansions of elements of lsi, but sho uld be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, s, colList) is equivalent to elt(x, expand(s), colList) but should be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, s1, ls2) is equivalent to elt(x, l1, l2) where li is obtained by appending expansions of elements of lsi, but sho uld be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(x, s1, s2) is equivalent to elt(x, expand(s1), expand(s2)) but should be more convenient and more efficient.

name: elt
doc: elt(agg,i) returns the i-th element.

name: elt
doc: elt(m, i, j) returns the element in the ith row and jth column of the array m error check to determine if indices are in proper ranges

name: elt
doc: elt(m, i, j, r) returns the element in the ith row and jth column of the array m, if m has an ith row and a jth column, and returns r otherwise

name: empty
doc: empty()$D creates an aggregate of type D with 0 elements. Note: The  $D can be dropped if understood by context, e.g. u: D := empty().

name: empty?
doc: empty?(u) tests if u has 0 elements.

name: eq?
doc: eq?(u, v) tests if u and v are same objects.

name: eval
doc: eval(f, x, v) replaces x by v in f.

name: eval
doc: eval(f, x = v) replaces x by v in f.

name: eval
doc: eval(f, [x1, ..., xn], [v1, ..., vn]) replaces xi by vi in f.

name: eval
doc: eval(f, [x1 = v1, ..., xn = vn]) replaces xi by vi in f.

name: every?
doc: every?(p, u) tests if p(x) is true for all elements x of u. Note: for collections, every?(p, u) = reduce(and, map(p, u), true, false). However, every?(p, u) returns as soon as it finds an element for which p gives false.

name: exquo
doc: exquo(f, g) creates the equivalent infix form.

name: exquo
doc: exquo(m, r) computes the exact quotient of the elements of m by r, returning "failed" if this is not possible.

name: extract
doc: extract(agg, parts) extracts parts of agg.

name: fill!
doc: fill!(m, r) fills m with r's

name: first
doc: first(agg) returns the first element of agg.

name: hash
doc: hash(s) calculates a hash code for s.

name: hashUpdate!
doc: hashUpdate!(hs, s) computes new HashState from old and s used for incremental computation of hash values. hashUpdate! mi ght destructively work on its first argument.

name: hermitian?
doc: \spad{hermitian?(m)} checks whether or not m is hermitian.

name: hessenberg
doc: hessenberg(m) computes the Hessenberg decomposition of the square matrix m.

name: horizConcat
doc: horizConcat(x, y) horizontally concatenates two arrays with an equal number of rows. The entries of y appear to the righ t of the entries of x. Error: if the arrays do not have the same number of rows.

name: horizConcat
doc: horizConcat(l) horizontally concatenates all members of l Error: if the arrays do not have the same number of rows.

name: horizSplit
doc: horizSplit(a, [n1, n2, ..., ni]) splits a into arrays having n1, ..., ni columns. Error: if number of columns of a is di fferent than n1 + ... + ni.

name: horizSplit
doc: horizSplit(a, n) splits a into n arrays of equal size column wise. Error: if number of columns of a is not divisible by n.

name: insert
doc: insert(l, elt, ind) inserts elt to the list l at index ind.

name: intersection
doc: intersection(agg1, agg2) is the intersection operator.

name: inverse
doc: inverse(m) computes the inverse of m. For example: \example{m:=jWSMatrix("\{\{a, b\}, \{b, a\}\}")@WSMAT(WSEXPR)} \example{inverse m}

name: inverse
doc: inverse(m) returns the inverse of the matrix m. If the matrix is not invertible, "failed" is returned. Error: if the mat rix is not square.

name: invertIfCan
doc: invertIfCan(m) returns the inverse of the matrix m. If the matrix is not invertible, "failed" is returned. Error: if the matrix is not square.

name: jWSAggregate
doc: jWSAggregate(list) constructs agg to a WSAggregate.

name: jWSInterpret
doc: jWSInterpret(form) interprets form.

name: jWSInterpret
doc:
jWSInterpret(Type|Form, Expr) interprets Expr to be of type Type or Form using the Wolfram Symbolic Language. For exampl e: 

**Examples**:
```fricas
jWSInterpret("Number","3.2")@WSREAL
jWSInterpret("Real","3.2")@WSREAL
jWSInterpret("L ocation","Lille")$WSEXPR See jWSExpr "$InterpreterTypes"
```

name: jWSInterpret
doc: jWSInterpret(form1,form2,form3) interprets forms.

name: jWSMatrix
doc: jWSMatrix(str) constructs str as a WSMatrix. str must be in the WS language (WS list of WS list(s)).

name: jlAbout
doc: jlAbout(obj) displays Julia information about obj if you have About.jl installed in Julia. In the Julia interpreter, ent er in the package management mode with ']', and issue: pkg> add "https://github.com/tecosaur/About.jl"

name: jlApply
doc:
jlApply(func, obj) applies the function func with obj as parameter and returns the result as a FriCAS JLObject. For exam ple, using JLMatrix(JLObjFloat64): 

**Examples**:
```fricas
M:=nrand(4,4);
jlApply("svd", M::JLMatrix(JLObjFloat64)).S shou ld be "equivalent" to svdvals(M).
```

name: jlApply
doc:
jlApply(func, obj1, obj2) applies the function func with obj1 and obj2 as parameters and returns the result as a FriCAS JLObject. For example (equivalent to map(cos, v)): 

**Examples**:
```fricas
v:=urand01(5)$JLVector(JLFloat)
jlApply("map", " cos", coerce v)
```

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, obj1, obj2, obj3) applies the function func with obj1, obj2 and obj3 as parameters and returns the result as a FriCAS JLObject.

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, obj1, obj2, obj3, obj4) applies the function func with obj1, obj2, obj3 and obj4 as parameters and returns the result as a FriCAS JLObject.

name: jlApply
doc: jlApply(func, obj1, obj2, obj3, obj4, obj5) applies the function func with obj1, obj2, obj3, obj4 and obj5 as parameters and returns the result as a FriCAS JLObject.

name: jlDisplay
doc: jlDisplay(v) pretty prints v (à la Julia).

name: jlDump
doc: jlDump(obj) dumps (shows) the Julia object (internal structure with type).

name: jlEval
doc: jlEval(expr) evaluates expr using the Wolfram Symbolic Transport Protocol.

name: jlFieldNames
doc: jlFieldNames(obj) returns the field names of obj.

name: jlGetField
doc: jlGetField(obj, sym) returns the property/element sym of obj.

name: jlGetJuliaIndex
doc: jlGetJuliaIndex(obj) returns the Julia indexed dictionary index referencing the object obj. Convenience function for use in the interpreter.

name: jlGetProperty
doc: jlGetProperty(obj, sym) returns the property/element sym of obj.

name: jlHead
doc: jlHead(expr) returns the Head type of expr.

name: jlId
doc: jlId(obj) returns the Julia indexed dictionary index referencing the object obj.

name: jlObject
doc:
jlObject() returns the internal Julia name of the Julia module used. For example: 

**Example**:

name: dSolve
doc:
dSolve(eq, func,var) solves the differential equation eq for the function(s) funcs with independent variable(s) vars. E xample: x:=jWSExpr x;



**Examples**:
```fricas
fx:=derivative(operator('f),0,x)
fprimex:=derivative(operator('f),1,x)
```


Exa mple: dSolve(fprimex + fx = a * sin(x)/cos(x),fx,x)

name: numericSolve

name: numericSum

name: one?

name: sphericalBesselY
doc: sphericalBesselY(n,z) returns the spherical Bessel of the second kind of z.

name: sphericalHankelH1
doc: sphericalHankelH1(n,z) returns the spherical Hankel function of the first kind of z.

name: sphericalHankelH2
doc: sphericalHankelH2(n,z) returns the spherical Hankel function of the second kind of z.

name: sphericalHarmonicY
doc: sphericalHarmonicY(l, m, theta, phi) returns the spherical harmonic Y function or evaluates it.

name: sqrt
doc: sqrt(x) returns the square root of x. The branch cut lies along the negative real axis, continuous with quadrant II.

name: squareFree
doc: squareFree(x) returns the square-free factorization of x i.e. such that the factors are pairwise relatively prime and ea ch has multiple prime factors.

name: squareFreePart
doc: squareFreePart(x) returns a product of prime factors of x each taken with multiplicity one.

name: squareFreePolynomial
doc: squareFreePolynomial(p) returns the square-free factorization of the univariate polynomial p.

name: stieltjesGamma
doc: stieltjesGamma(n) returns the n-th Stieltjes constant.

name: stieltjesGamma
doc: stieltjesGamma(n,a) returns the generalized n-th Stieltjes constant.

name: string
doc: string(jt) returns the string representation of jt.

name: struveH
doc: struveH(v, z) is the Struve H function.

name: struveL
doc: struveL(v, z) is the Struve L function defined by the formula struveL(v, z) = -%i^exp(-v*%pi*%i/2)*struveH(v, %i*z).

name: subResultants
doc: subResultants(p1,p2,x) returns the subresultant of p1 and p2 with respect to x.

name: subst
doc: subst(f, k = g) replaces the kernel k by g formally in f.

name: subst
doc: subst(f, [k1..., kn], [g1, ..., gn]) replaces the kernels k1, ..., kn by g1, ..., gn formally in f.

name: subst
doc: subst(f, [k1 = g1, ..., kn = gn]) replaces the kernels k1, ..., kn by g1, ..., gn formally in f.

name: subtractIfCan
doc: subtractIfCan(x, y) returns an element z such that z+y=x or "failed" if no such element exists.

name: sum
doc: sum(f(n),range) returns the sum f(imin) + ... + f(imax) defined by the list range, for example \example{jWSExpr("\{i, imin, imax\}")}. See Wolfram Language specifications.

name: sum
doc: sum(f(n),n, a..b) returns the sum f(a) + ... + f(b).

name: sum
doc: sum(f(n),n) returns the indefinite sum of f(n).

name: sum
doc: sum(expr) creates the form prefixing expr by a capital sigma.

name: sum
doc: sum(expr, lowerlimit, upperlimit) creates the form prefixing expr by a capital sigma with both a lowerlimit and upperlim it.

name: summation
doc: summation(f(n), n = a..b) returns f(a) + ... + f(b) as a formal sum.

name: summation
doc: summation(f(n), n) returns the formal sum S(n) which verifies S(n+1) - S(n) = f(n).

name: symmetricPolynomial
doc: symmetricPolynomial(n,lvars) returns the n-th elementary symmetric polynomial with respect to variables in lvars.

name: symmetricReduction
doc: symmetricReduction(f,lvars) returns a pair of polynomials representing f = p+q where p is a symmetric polynomial, q the remainder.

name: symmetricReduction
doc: symmetricReduction(f, lvars, replnt) returns a pair of polynomials representing f = p+q where p is a symmetric polynomial, q the remainder where variables in p replaced by the ones in replnt.

name: symmetricReduction
doc: symmetricReduction(f, lvars, replnt) returns a pair of polynomials representing f = p+q where p is a symmetric polynomia l, q the remainder where variables in p replaced by the ones in replnt.

name: take
doc: take(l,i) returns the first i elements.

name: tan
doc: tan(x) returns the tangent of x.

name: tanh
doc: tanh(x) returns the hyperbolic tangent of x.

name: toExpression
doc: toExpression(expr) converts expr to a WS expression and evaluates it.

name: toExpression
doc: toExpression(expr, form) converts expr to a WS expression and evaluates it with output in the format form.

name: toExpression
doc: toExpression(expr, form, h) converts expr to a WS expression and evaluates it with output in the format form but wrapping the head with h. `Hold` for example.

name: toString
doc: toString(expr, form) returns the string representation of expr with WS language format form.

name: toString
doc: toString(obj) returns the string representation of obj.

name: together
doc: together(expr) puts together terms over a common denominator cancelling common factors.

name: tower
doc: tower(f) returns all the kernels appearing in f, no matter what their levels are.

name: tower
doc: tower([f1,...,fn]) returns all the kernels appearing in f1, ..., fn no matter what their levels are.

name: trace
doc: trace(a) returns the trace of the regular representation of a with respect to any basis.

name: traceMatrix
doc: traceMatrix() is the n-by-n matrix ( Tr(vi * vj) ), where v1, ..., vn are the elements of the fixed basis.

name: traceMatrix
doc: traceMatrix([v1, .., vn]) is the n-by-n matrix ( Tr(vi * vj) )

name: traditionalForm
doc: traditionalForm(expr) returns a traditional form of expr i.e. its WS 'TraditionalForm'.

name: trigExpand
doc: trigExpand(expr) tries to expand (hyperbolic) trigonometric functions in expr.

name: trigFactor
doc: trigFactor(expr) factors (hyperbolic) trigonometric functions in expr.

name: trigFactorList
doc: trigFactorList(expr) returns a list of factors of (hyperbolic) trigonometric functions in expr.

name: trigReduce
doc: trigReduce(expr) reduces power and products of trigonometric functions.

name: trigToExp
doc: trigToExp(expr) returns expr with (hyperbolic) trigonometric functions converted to, eventually complex, exponentials.

name: union
doc: union(agg1, agg2) is the union set operator. Elements are sorted on output.

name: unit?
doc: unit?(x) tests whether x is a unit, i.e. is invertible.

name: unitCanonical
doc: unitCanonical(x) returns unitNormal(x).canonical.

name: unitNormal
doc: unitNormal(x) tries to choose a canonical element from the associate class of x. The attribute canonicalUnitNormal, if a sserted, means that the "canonical" element is the same across all associates of x if unitNormal(x) = [u, c, a] then u*c = x, a*u = 1.

name: unitStep
doc: unitStep(x) is 0 for x less than 0, 1 for x bigger or equal 0.

name: univariate
doc: univariate(f, k) returns f viewed as a univariate fraction in k.

name: values
doc: values(expr) returns the values elements in expr.

name: variables
doc: variables(p) returns the list of variables in p.

name: variables
doc: variables(f) returns the list of all the variables of f.

name: variables
doc: variables([f1, ..., fn]) returns the list of all the variables of f1, ..., fn.

name: weberE
doc: weberE(v,n,z) is the associated Weber E function.

name: weberE
doc: weberE(v, z) is the Weber E function.

name: weierstrassP
doc: weierstrassP(g2, g3, z) is the Weierstrass P function.

name: weierstrassPInverse
doc: weierstrassPInverse(g2, g3, z) is the inverse of Weierstrass P function, defined by the formula \spad{WeierstrassP(g2, g3, WeierstrassPInverse(g2, g3, z)) = z}.

name: weierstrassPPrime
doc: weierstrassPPrime(g2, g3, z) is the derivative of the Weierstrass P function.

name: weierstrassSigma
doc: weierstrassSigma(g2, g3, z) is the Weierstrass sigma function.

name: weierstrassZeta
doc: weierstrassZeta(g2, g3, z) is the Weierstrass Zeta function.

name: whittakerM
doc: whittakerM(k,m,x) computes the Whittaker function M of x.

name: whittakerW
doc: whittakerW(k,m,z) computes the Whittaker function W of z.

name: wilsonW
doc: wilsonW(n, a, b, c, d, z) is the Wilson polynomial.

name: zernikeR
doc: zernikeR(n, m, x) returns the Zernike radial polynomial or evaluates it at x if x is a number.

name: zero?
doc: zero? x tries to determine if x is 0. For example: \example{expr:=0$WSEXPR/1*sqrt(17::WSEXPR); zero? expr}

name: zeroOf
doc: zeroOf(p) returns y such that p(y) = 0. The value y is expressed in terms of radicals if possible, and otherwise as an i mplicit algebraic quantity. Error: if p has more than one variable.

name: zeroOf
doc: zeroOf(p, y) returns y such that p(y) = 0. The value y is expressed in terms of radicals if possible, and otherwise as a n implicit algebraic quantity which displays as 'y.

name: zeroOf
doc: zeroOf(p) returns y such that p(y) = 0. If possible, y is expressed in terms of radicals. Otherwise it is an implicit al gebraic quantity. Error: if p has more than one variable y.

name: zeroOf
doc: zeroOf(p) returns y such that p(y) = 0; if possible, y is expressed in terms of radicals. Otherwise it is an implicit al gebraic quantity.

name: zeroOf
doc: zeroOf(p, y) returns y such that p(y) = 0; if possible, y is expressed in terms of radicals. Otherwise it is an implicit algebraic quantity which displays as 'y.

name: zerosOf
doc: zerosOf(p) returns [y1, ..., yn] such that p(yi) = 0. The yi's are expressed in radicals if possible. Note: the returned values y1, ..., yn contain new symbols which are bound in the interpreter to the respective values. Error: if p has mor e than one variable.

name: zerosOf
doc: zerosOf(p, y) returns [y1, ..., yn] such that p(yi) = 0. The yi's are expressed in radicals if possible, and otherwise a s implicit algebraic quantities containing new symbols which display as '%z0, '%z1, ...; The new symbols are bound in th e interpreter to the respective values.

name: zerosOf
doc: zerosOf(p) returns [y1, ..., yn] such that p(yi) = 0. The yi's are expressed in radicals if possible. Otherwise they are implicit algebraic quantities containing new symbols. The new symbols are bound in the interpreter to the respective va lues. Error: if p has more than one variable y.

name: zerosOf
doc: zerosOf(p) returns [y1, ..., yn] such that p(yi) = 0. The yi's are expressed in radicals if possible. Otherwise they are implicit algebraic quantities containing new symbols. The new symbols are bound in the interpreter to the respective va lues.

name: WSNumericalSpecialFunctions
doc: Julia Wolfram Symbolic numerical special functions using the MathLink Julia package.

name: Beta
doc: Beta(x, y) is \spad{Gamma(x) * Gamma(y)/Gamma(x+y)}.

name: Beta
doc: Beta(z, a, b) is the incomplete Beta function.

name: Beta
doc: Beta(x, y) is Gamma(x) * Gamma(y)/Gamma(x+y).

name: EiEn
doc: EiEn(n,z) returns the exponential integral En of z.

name: Gamma
doc: Gamma(z) is the Euler Gamma function.

name: Gamma
doc: Gamma(a, z) is the incomplete Gamma function.

name: Gamma
doc: Gamma(a,z1,z2) computes the generalized incomplete Gamma function.

name: airyAi
doc: airyAi(z) is the Airy function \spad{Ai(z)}.

name: airyAiPrime
doc: airyAiPrime(z) is the derivative of the Airy function \spad{Ai(z)}.

name: airyAiZero
doc: airyAiZero(n) is the n-th zero function of the Airy function \spad{Ai(z)}.

name: airyAiZero
doc: airyAiZero(n,x) is the n-th zero function of the Airy function \spad{Ai(z)} smaller than x.

name: airyBi
doc: airyBi(z) is the Airy function \spad{Bi(z)}.

name: airyBiPrime
doc: airyBiPrime(z) is the derivative of the Airy function \spad{Bi(z)}.

name: airyBiZero
doc: airyBiZero(n) is the n-th zero function of the Airy function \spad{Bi(z)}.

name: airyBiZero
doc: airyBiZero(n,x) is the n-th zero function of the Airy function \spad{Bi(z)} smaller than x.

name: angerJ
doc: angerJ(v, z) is the Anger J function.

name: angerJ
doc: angerJ(v, n, z) is the associated Anger J function.

name: barnesG
doc: barnesG(z) computes the Barnes G-function of z.

name: besselI
doc: besselI(v, z) is the modified Bessel function of the first kind.

name: besselJ
doc: besselJ(v, z) is the Bessel function of the first kind.

name: besselJZero
doc: besselJZero(n,x) returns the n-th zero of the Bessel J n-th function.

name: besselK
doc: besselK(v, z) is the modified Bessel function of the second kind.

name: besselY
doc: besselY(v, z) is the Bessel function of the second kind.

name: besselYZero
doc: besselYZero(n,x) returns the n-th zero of the Bessel Y n-th function.

name: betaRegularized
doc: betaRegularized(z,a,b) computes the regularized incomplete Beta function.

name: charlierC
doc: charlierC(n, a, z) is the Charlier polynomial

name: chebyshevT
doc: chebyshevT(n, z) evaluates the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind at z.

name: chebyshevU
doc: chebyshevU(n, expr) evaluates the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind at z.

name: conjugate
doc: conjugate(z) is the conjugate of the complex number z.

name: coulombF
doc: coulombF(l,eta,ro) is the regular Coulomb wave function.

name: coulombG
doc: coulombG(l,eta,ro) is the irregular Coulomb wave function.

name: coulombH1
doc: coulombH1(l,eta,ro) is the incoming irregular Coulomb wave function H^(+).

name: coulombH2
doc: coulombH2(l,eta,ro) is the incoming irregular Coulomb wave function H^(-).

name: dawson
doc: dawson(x) computes the Dawson integral of x.

name: dedekindEta
doc: dedekindEta(tau) computes the Dedekind eta modular function.

name: digamma
doc: digamma(z) is the logarithmic derivative of \spad{Gamma(z)} (often written \spad{psi(z)} in the literature).

name: digamma
doc: digamma(n,z) is the n-th derivative of the digamma function.

name: diracDelta
doc: diracDelta(x) returns the Dirac delta function of x.

name: dirichletEta
doc: dirichletEta(z) computes the Dirichlet eta function of z.

name: dirichletL
doc: dirichletL(k,j,s) returns Dirichlet L-function of s, modulus k, index j.

name: ellipticE
doc: ellipticE(z) computes the complete elliptic integral of the second kind.

name: ellipticE
doc: ellipticE(phi,m) computes the elliptic integral of the second kind.

name: ellipticF
doc: ellipticF(phi,m) computes the elliptic integral of the first kind.

name: ellipticK
doc: ellipticK(m) computes the complete elliptic integral of the first kind.

name: ellipticPi
doc: ellipticPi(n,m) computes the complete elliptic integral of the third kind.

name: ellipticPi
doc: ellipticPi(n,phi,m) computes the elliptic integral of the third kind.

name: ellipticTheta
doc: ellipticTheta(a, u, q) computes the theta function, a ranges from 1 to 4.

name: ellipticThetaPrime
doc: ellipticThetaPrime(a, u, q) computes the derivative of the theta function, a ranges from 1 to 4.

name: fibonacci
doc: fibonacci(n, z) evaluates the Fibonacci polynomial at z.

name: gammaRegularized
doc: gammaRegularized(a,z) computes the regularized incomplete Gamma function.

name: gegenbauerC
doc: gegenbauerC(n,z) evaluates the renormalized form of the Gegenbauer polynomial at z.

name: gegenbauerC
doc: gegenbauerC(n,lambda,z) evaluates the Gegenbauer polynomial at z.

name: gudermannian
doc: gudermannian(z) computes the Gudermannian of z.

name: hankelH1
doc: hankelH1(v, z) is the first Hankel function (Bessel function of the third kind).

name: hankelH2
doc: hankelH2(v, z) is the second Hankel function (Bessel function of the third kind).

name: haversine
doc: haversine(z) computes the Haversine of z.

name: hermiteH
doc: hermiteH(n, z) evaluates the Hermite polynomial at z.

name: hurwitzLerchPhi
doc: hurwitzLerchPhi(z,s,a) computes the Hurwitz-Lerch transcendent phi function.

name: hurwitzZeta
doc: hurwitzZeta(s,a) computes the Hurwitz zeta.

name: hyperFactorial
doc: hyperFactorial(n) computes the hyperfactorial of n.

name: hypergeometric0F1
doc: hypergeometric0F1(a,z) is the hypergeometric 0F1.

name: hypergeometric0F1Regularized
doc: hypergeometric0F1Regularized(a,z) is the regularized hypergeometric 0F1.

name: hypergeometric1F1
doc: hypergeometric1F1(a,b,z) is the Kummer confluent hypergeometric function 1F1.

name: hypergeometric1F1Regularized
doc: hypergeometric1F1Regularized(a,b,z) is the regularized confluent hypergeometric function 1F1.

name: hypergeometricU
doc: hypergeometricU(a,b,z) is the confluent hypergeometric function U.

name: inverseBetaRegularized
doc: inverseBetaRegularized(s,a,b) computes the Beta inverse.

name: inverseErf
doc: inverseErf(z) computes the inverse error function of z.

name: inverseErfc
doc: inverseErfc(z) computes the inverse complementary error function of z.

name: inverseGammaRegularized
doc: inverseGammaRegularized(a,s) computes the Gamma inverse.

name: inverseGudermannian
doc: inverseGudermannian(z) computes the inverse Gudermannian of z.

name: inverseHaversine
doc: inverseHaversine(z) computes the inverse Haversine of z.

name: inverseJacobiCn
doc: inverseJacobiCn(nu, m) computes the inverse Jacobi's CN elliptic function.

name: inverseJacobiSn
doc: inverseJacobiSn(nu, m) computes the inverse Jacobi's SN elliptic function.

name: jacobiAmplitude
doc: jacobiAmplitude(u,m) computes the amplitude function am.

name: jacobiCn
doc: jacobiCn(z, m) is the Jacobi elliptic cn function, defined by \spad{jacobiCn(z, m)^2 + jacobiSn(z, m)^2 = 1} and \spad{jacobiCn(0, m) = 1}.

name: jacobiDn
doc: jacobiDn(z, m) is the Jacobi elliptic dn function, defined by \spad{jacobiDn(z, m)^2 + m*jacobiSn(z, m)^2 = 1} and \spad{jacobiDn(0, m) = 1}.

name: jacobiP
doc: jacobiP(n, a, b, z) evaluates the Jacobi polynomial at z.

name: jacobiSn
doc: jacobiSn(z, m) is the Jacobi elliptic sn function, defined by the formula \spad{jacobiSn(ellipticF(z, m), m) = z}.

name: jacobiTheta
doc: jacobiTheta(n, z, m) are the Jacobi theta functions.

name: jacobiZeta
doc: jacobiZeta(z, m) is the Jacobi elliptic zeta function, defined by \spad{D(jacobiZeta(z, m), z) = jacobiDn(z, m)^2 - ellipticE(m)/ellipticK(m)} and \spad{jacobiZeta(0, m) = 0}.

name: jacobiZeta
doc: ellipticPi(n,phi,m) computes the elliptic integral of the third kind.

name: kelvinBei
doc: kelvinBei(v, z) is the Kelvin bei function defined by equality \spad{kelvinBei(v, z) = imag(besselJ(v, exp(3*Rpi*Ri/4)*z))} for z and v real.

name: kelvinBer
doc: kelvinBer(v, z) is the Kelvin ber function defined by equality \spad{kelvinBer(v, z) = real(besselJ(v, exp(3*Rpi*Ri/4)*z))} for z and v real.

name: kelvinKei
doc: kelvinKei(v, z) is the Kelvin kei function defined by equality \spad{kelvinKei(v, z) = imag(exp(-v*Rpi*Ri/2)*besselK(v, exp(Rpi*Ri/4)*z))} for z and v real.

name: kelvinKer
doc: kelvinKer(v, z) is the Kelvin ker function defined by equality \spad{kelvinKer(v, z) = real(exp(-v*Rpi*Ri/2)*besselK(v, exp(Rpi*Ri/4)*z))} for z and v real.

name: kleinInvariantJ
doc: kleinInvariantJ(tau) computes the Klein's absolute invariant.

name: laguerreL
doc: laguerreL(n, z) evaluates the Laguerre polynomial at z.

name: laguerreL
doc: laguerreL(n, a, z) evaluates the generalized Laguerre polynomial a z.

name: lambertW
doc: lambertW(z) = w is the principal branch of the solution to the equation \spad{we^w = z}.

name: lambertW
doc: lambertW(k,z) returns the k-th solution to LambertW function.

name: legendreP
doc: legendreP(nu, mu, z) is the Legendre P function.

name: legendreP
doc: legendreP(n, z) evaluates the Legendre polynomial of the first kind at z.

name: legendreQ
doc: legendreQ(nu, mu, z) is the Legendre Q function.

name: legendreQ
doc: legendreQ(n, z) returns the Legendre function of the second kind.

name: lerchPhi
doc: lerchPhi(z, s, a) is the Lerch Phi function.

name: logBarnesG
doc: logBarnesG(z) is the logarithm of Barnes-G.

name: logGamma
doc: logGamma(z) returns the log-Gamma of z.

name: lommelS1
doc: lommelS1(mu, nu, z) is the Lommel s function.

name: lommelS2
doc: lommelS2(mu, nu, z) is the Lommel S function.

name: mathieuC
doc: mathieuC(a,q,z) is the even Mathieu function with characteristic a and parameter q.

name: mathieuCPrime
doc: mathieuCPrime(a,q,z) derivative of the even Mathieu function.

name: mathieuCharacteristicA
doc: mathieuCharacteristicA(r,q) returns the characteristic for even Mathieu function.

name: mathieuCharacteristicB
doc: mathieuCharacteristicB(r,q) returns the characteristic for odd Mathieu function.

name: mathieuCharacteristicExponent
doc: mathieuCharacteristicExponent(a,q) returns the characteristic exponent of the Mathieu function.

name: mathieuS
doc: mathieuS(b,q,z) is the odd Mathieu function with characteristic b and parameter q.

name: mathieuSPrime
doc: mathieuSPrime(b,q,z) derivative of the odd Mathieu function.

name: modularLambda
doc: modularLambda(tau) computes the lambda modular function.

name: parabolicCylinderD
doc: parabolicCylinderD(nu,z) computes the parabolic cylinder function D of z.

name: pochhammer
doc: pochhammer(a,n) returns the Pochhammer symbol.

name: polygamma
doc: polygamma(k, z) is the \spad{k-th} derivative of \spad{digamma(z)}, (often written \spad{psi(k, z)} in the literature).

name: polylog
doc: polylog(s, z) is the polylogarithm of order s at z.

name: polylog
doc: polylog(n,p,z) is the Nielsen generalized polylogarithm function.

name: qBinomial
doc: qBinomial(n,m,q) returns the q-analog of binomial coefficient.

name: qFactorial
doc: qFactorial(z,q) returns the q-analog of factorial of z.

name: qGamma
doc: qGamma(z,q) returns the q-analog of Euler Gamma of z.

name: qPochhammer
doc: qPochhammer(z,q) returns the q-Pochhammer symbol of z.

name: qPochhammer
doc: qPochhammer(z,q,n) returns the q-Pochhammer symbol of z.

name: qPolyGamma
doc: qPolyGamma(z,q) returns the q-digamma of z.

name: qPolyGamma
doc: qPolyGamma(n,z,q) returns the n-th derivative of the q-digamma function of z.

name: ramanujanTau
doc: ramanujanTau(n) returns the Ramanujan tau of n.

doc: ramanujanTauL(s) computes the Ramanujan tau Dirichlet L-function of s.

doc: ramanujanTauTheta(z) returns the Ramanujan tau theta of z.

name: ramanujanTauZ
doc: ramanujanTauZ(t) computes the Ramanujan tau Z-function of t.

name: riemannSiegelTheta
doc: riemannSiegelTheta(t) returns the Riemann-Siegel theta function of t.

name: riemannSiegelZ
doc: riemannSiegelZ(t) computes the Riemann-Siegel Z function of t.

name: riemannZeta
doc: riemannZeta(z) is the Riemann Zeta function.

name: riemannZeta
doc: riemannZeta(s,a) is the generalized Riemann Zeta function.

name: sign
doc: sign(x) is 1 if x is positive, -1 if x is negative, 0 if x equals 0.

name: sphericalBesselY
doc: sphericalBesselY(n,z) returns the spherical Bessel of the second kind of z.

name: sphericalHankelH1
doc: sphericalHankelH1(n,z) returns the spherical Hankel of the first kind of z.

doc: sphericalHankelH2(n,z) computes the spherical Hankel of the second kind of z.

name: sphericalHarmonicY
doc: sphericalHarmonicY(l, m, theta, phi) returns the spherical harmonic Y or evaluates it.

name: stieltjesGamma

name: weberE
doc: weberE(v, n, z) is the associated Weber E function.

doc: weierstrassP(g2, g3, z) is the Weierstrass P function.

name: weierstrassPPrime
doc: weierstrassPPrime(g2, g3, z) is the derivative of Weierstrass P function.

doc: weierstrassSigma(g2, g3, z) is the Weierstrass sigma function.

name: weierstrassZeta
doc: weierstrassZeta(g2, g3, z) is the Weierstrass Zeta function.

name: whittakerM
doc: whittakerM(k, m, z) is the Whittaker M function.

name: whittakerW
doc: whittakerW(k, m, z) is the Whittaker W function.

name: zernikeR
doc: zernikeR(n, m, z) evaluates the Zernike radial polynomial at z.

name: WSUtilityFunctions
doc: Julia Wolfram Symbolic utility functions using the MathLink Julia package.

name: fourierMatrix
doc: fourierMatrix(n) returns the n x n Fourier matrix.

name: gaussianMatrix
doc: gaussianMatrix(r) returns the Gaussian matrix with radius r. For example: \example{gaussianMatrix "2.2"}

name: hankelMatrix
doc: hankelMatrix(n) returns the square Hankel matrix with integer coefficients.

name: hilbertMatrix
doc: hilbertMatrix(n) returns the square Hilbert matrix.

name: identityMatrix
doc: identityMatrix(n) returns the identity matrix of size n.

name: jWSDateObject
doc: jWSDateObject() returns the WSExpression object of the local date and time.

name: jWSDateObject
doc: jWSDateObject(expr) returns the WSExpression object of the date from expr.

name: jWSDateObject
doc: jWSDateObject(date,type) returns the WSExpression object of the date and type, for example "Month".

name: jWSRange
doc: jWSRange(n) returns a WSList that ranges from 1 to n. For example: \example{jWSRange(10)@WSLIST(WSINT)}

name: jWSRange
doc: jWSRange(n,m) returns a WSList that ranges from n to m.

name: jWSRange
doc: jWSRange(n,m) returns a WSList that ranges from n to m.

name: jWSRange
doc: jWSRange(n,m,d) returns a WSList that ranges from n to m with step d.

name: jlWSDateString
doc: jlWSDateString() returns the WSExpression string of the local date and time. For example: \example{toString jlWSDateString()}

name: jlWSDateString
doc: jlWSDateString(expr) returns the WSExpression string of the date from a WS date object. For example: \example{jlWSDateString jWSExpr "Tomorrow"}

name: jlWSDateString
doc: jlWSDateString(expr, form) returns WSExpression string of the date from a WS date object with WS format form. For example: \example{jlWSDateString(jWSExpr("Now"), jWSExpr("Entity[_"Language_", _"French::367gk_"]"))}

name: jlWSDocumentation
doc: jlWSDocumentation(sym) prints WS information about the symbol sym. Note that the WS language is preferable. Trivial implementation. For example: \example{jlWSDocumentation sin} \example{jlWSDocumentation ArcSin}

name: jlWSExport
doc: jlWSExport(file.ext, obj) exports the object obj to the file file.ext. The extension ext will determine the saved format. A WS expression for example can be exported in an image file, it will be saved in the WS 'StandardForm' whereas in FriCAS it is displayed in WS 'OutputForm': \example{x:=jWSExpr(x);jlWSExport("legendreP.png", legendreP(7, x))}

name: jlWSExportString
doc: jlWSExportString(expr, form) returns the string representation of expr in the specified format. Use toString or string to obtain the FriCAS String. For example: \example{jWSExpr \"Probability[x < 0, x \\[Distributed] NormalDistribution[]]\"} \example{jWSExpr \"Probability[x < 1, x \\[Distributed] NormalDistribution[]]\"} \example{string jlWSExportString(%,jWSString "TeX")}

name: jlWSFileFormat
doc: jlWSFileFormat(src) tries to determine the format of the source src from its content. Can be used with jWSImport. For example: \example{jlWSFileFormat("examples/customers-100.csv")}

name: jlWSFileFormat
doc: jlWSFileFormat(src, list(form)) tries to determine the format of the source src from its content using the list of formats form. Returns WS None if no format is found. Can be used with jWSImport. For example: \spad{jlWSFileFormat("examples/customers-100.csv",jWSExpr "{_"CSV_",_"TSV_"}")}

name: jlWSImport
doc: jlWSImport(src) imports the source src. For example: \example{file:=jlWSImport jWSString "examples/customers-100.csv";} \example{jlWSDateString(file.2.11)}

name: jlWSImport
doc: jlWSImport(myfile, form) imports the file myfile with format form. For example: \example{file:=jlWSImport(jWSString("examples/customers-100.csv"), jWSString "CSV");}

name: jlWSPlot
doc: jlWSPlot(expr, options) is the WS plot function. Since it should be run in a Wolfram notebook or any other supported graphical interfaces, the Wolfram Jupyter "plugin" for example, it is left to the user for testing purposes. The following uses the jlWSExport function: \example{x:=jWSExpr(x);opt:=jWSList [x,-5,5]} \example{jlWSExport("sin.png", jlWSPlot(sin(x),opt))}

name: jlWSSeedRandom!
doc: jlWSSeedRandom!(n) reseeds the random number generator with n as seed. Returns the random generator state.

name: jlWSSnippet
doc: jlWSSnippet(expr, n) returns the first (or last) n snippets of the WSExpression expr. For example: \example{jlWSSnippet(jlWSImport jWSString "http://www.fricas.org/",-2)}

name: urand01Complex
doc: urand01Complex(n) returns a Julia WS vector with uniformly distributed random complex elements in the unit square. Convenience function.

name: urand01Complex

name: urand01Complex
doc: urand01Complex(rows,cols) returns a Julia WS matrix with uniformly distributed random complex elements in the unit squar e. Convenience function.

name: urand01Real
doc: urand01Real(n) returns a Julia WS vector with uniformly distributed random elements in the range 0..1. Convenience function.

name: urand01Real
doc: urand01Real(rows,cols) returns a Julia WS matrix with uniformly distributed random elements in the range 0..1. Convenience function.
